### additional:replit-agent | Replit Agent

Source URL: https://docs.replit.com/replitai/agent

Modules: M2, AI

Priority: optional

Focus: A browser-based AI builder that turns plain-language descriptions into deployed apps, data visualizations and slides. It plans, writes code, sets up infrastructure and tests, with a Plan mode for reviewing the task list first. Free Mode covers everyday use, and paid Power and Max modes handle harder work.

Teaching Suggestion: For teams that want an interactive dashboard to accompany their blog post without managing hosting.

Cautions: Pricing (https://replit.com/pricing, 2026-10-23): Core $20/month ($18 annual), Pro $100 ($90), Enterprise custom. Free or Starter details were not stated clearly on the pricing page. No education offer listed.

### additional:harper-reed-llm-codegen-workflow | My LLM codegen workflow atm

Source URL: https://harper.blog/2025/02/16/my-llm-codegen-workflow-atm/

Modules: AI

Priority: core

Focus: A widely cited workflow: brainstorm a spec with an LLM asking one question at a time (spec.md), have a reasoning model write a step-by-step plan and prompts (prompt_plan.md, todo.md), then execute step by step with tests. Brownfield work uses repomix to pack context for review and for finding missing tests.

Teaching Suggestion: Assigned reading. Students apply the spec, plan, execute loop to their team project and commit spec.md and todo.md to the repo.

Cautions: Published February 16, 2025. Follow-up 'Basic Claude Code' (May 8, 2025): https://harper.blog/2025/05/08/basic-claude-code/ (link from the post).

Rights or Access: open

### additional:willison-git-with-coding-agents | Using Git with coding agents

Source URL: https://simonwillison.net/guides/agentic-engineering-patterns/using-git-with-coding-agents/

Modules: AI, M1

Priority: recommended

Focus: Git as the safety net for agent work. Have agents init repos, commit and review recent commits to load context; explain merge, rebase and squash; resolve conflicts with tests; recover lost work from the reflog; write git-bisect test scripts; and tidy history.

Teaching Suggestion: Short reading for the GitHub-workflow lab: commit before every agent run, and review the diff before accepting.

Cautions: Last updated March 21, 2026 (from page metadata).

Rights or Access: open

Source URL: https://google.github.io/eng-practices/review/reviewer/looking-for.html

Modules: AI

Priority: recommended

Focus: Google's reviewer checklist: design, functionality and edge cases, complexity and over-engineering, tests that actually fail when code breaks, naming, and comments that explain why.

Teaching Suggestion: Adapt it into the course's 'AI-generated analysis code review checklist', adding data-specific items: row counts, joins, missing values, units, and reproducing headline numbers.

### additional:pandera | pandera: statistical data testing for DataFrames

Source URL: https://github.com/unionai-oss/pandera

Modules: M2, M3, AI

Priority: recommended

Focus: A lightweight library for declaring DataFrame schemas (types, ranges, allowed values) and validating pandas or polars data with `schema.validate()`. Failures surface silent errors that AI-written cleaning code can introduce.

Teaching Suggestion: Exercise: students ask the agent to write the cleaning step and also a pandera schema plus pytest assertions, then deliberately break the data to check that the tests catch it.

Cautions: Docs: https://pandera.readthedocs.io. In recent versions use `import pandera.pandas as pa`; the top-level import is deprecated. Pair with pytest: https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/getting-started.html (fetched).

Rights or Access: open

### additional:turing-way-reproducible-research | The Turing Way: Guide for Reproducible Research

Source URL: https://book.the-turing-way.org/reproducible-research/reproducible-research

Modules: M1, AI

Priority: recommended

Focus: An open handbook by more than 300 contributors. Its chapters on version control, testing, reproducible environments and code review give a vendor-neutral base for checking any analysis, including AI-written code.

Teaching Suggestion: Link the Testing (https://book.the-turing-way.org/reproducible-research/testing) and Reproducible Environments (https://book.the-turing-way.org/reproducible-research/renv) chapters from the project-requirements page.

Cautions: Subchapter URLs come from the fetched page. CC BY lets the wiki adapt excerpts with attribution.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:good-enough-practices | Good enough practices in scientific computing

Source URL: https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005510

Modules: M1, AI

Priority: recommended

Focus: A minimal set of practices for newcomers: keep raw data unchanged, script every processing step, write short well-named functions, state dependencies explicitly, use a consistent project layout with README, LICENSE and CITATION files, and use version control.

Teaching Suggestion: Academic anchor for the team-project repo rubric. Students can have the agent scaffold this layout.

### additional:uv-python | uv: Python package and project manager

Source URL: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/

Modules: AI, M1

Priority: recommended

Focus: A fast Rust-based replacement for pip, virtualenv, pip-tools and pyenv. It provides a universal lockfile (`uv lock`, `uv sync`), `uv run` for isolated execution, and inline script dependency metadata (`uv add --script`).

Teaching Suggestion: Require a uv lockfile (or requirements.txt for Colab) in team repos, so the analysis an agent produced on one laptop reruns on the grader's machine.

Cautions: Repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv. I did not verify the license from the fetched page. In Colab, students can instead pin versions in a requirements.txt and run `pip install -r`.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:owasp-llm-top10-2025 | OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025

Source URL: https://genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/

Modules: AI, M7, M8

Priority: core

Focus: The standard list of LLM application risks: LLM01 prompt injection, LLM02 sensitive information disclosure, LLM03 supply chain, LLM04 data and model poisoning, LLM05 improper output handling, LLM06 excessive agency, LLM07 system prompt leakage, LLM08 vector and embedding weaknesses, LLM09 misinformation, LLM10 unbounded consumption.

Teaching Suggestion: Security page backbone. Map LLM01, LLM02, LLM06 and LLM09 to concrete student behaviors with agents and data.

Cautions: Agent-specific companion: 'OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026' (published December 9, 2025; https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-agentic-applications-for-2026/, fetched). Its landing page does not list the ten items; the PDF is at https://genai.owasp.org/download/52117/?tmstv=1765059207 (not opened).

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:willison-lethal-trifecta | The lethal trifecta for AI agents: private data, untrusted content, and external communication

Source URL: https://simonwillison.net/2025/Jun/16/the-lethal-trifecta/

Modules: AI

Priority: core

Focus: An agent that combines access to private data, exposure to untrusted content and the ability to communicate externally can be steered by prompt injection into leaking data. Guardrails help only partly, so avoid giving one agent all three.

Teaching Suggestion: The single most teachable security concept. Students check their own setup (for example customer CSV + web browsing + MCP email = all three) against it.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:greshake-indirect-prompt-injection | Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.12173

Modules: AI, M8

Priority: optional

Focus: The foundational paper on indirect prompt injection. Instructions hidden in content an LLM retrieves can hijack the application, causing data theft, worming and contamination of information ecosystems. Demonstrated against Bing Chat and code-completion engines.

Teaching Suggestion: Academic citation for the security page, and for M5's point that scraped social-media text may itself contain injected instructions.

Cautions: The arXiv page lists no venue. The paper is widely cited as appearing at ACM AISec 2023, which I did not verify here.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:perry-insecure-code-ai-assistants | Do Users Write More Insecure Code with AI Assistants?

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.03622

Modules: AI, M6

Priority: recommended

Focus: In a user study, participants with an AI assistant wrote significantly less secure code yet were more confident it was secure. Participants who trusted the AI less and refined their prompts more produced fewer vulnerabilities.

Teaching Suggestion: Evidence for the course norm 'confidence is not correctness'. Pair it with an in-class exercise auditing AI-generated code.

Cautions: The arXiv page shows the ACM DOI but not the venue name. CCS 2023 is inferred from the DOI and should be confirmed before citing.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:uci-online-retail-ii | Online Retail II

Modules: M1, M2, M4

Priority: core

Focus: 1,067,371 invoice lines from a UK online retailer, Dec 2009 to Dec 2011, in a single 43.5 MB xlsx file (invoice, stock code, quantity, price, customer ID, country).

Teaching Suggestion: Default dataset for M2 cleaning and visualization and for M4 RFM segmentation and CLV exercises. It is small enough for Colab.

Cautions: The original Online Retail (I) has 541,909 rows (Dec 2010 to Dec 2011), 22.6 MB, CC BY 4.0, DOI 10.24432/C5BW33, at https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/352/online+retail . Expect cancellations/returns and missing customer IDs to clean; check these on load.

### additional:dunnhumby-source-files | dunnhumby Source Files: The Complete Journey, Breakfast at the Frat, Carbo-Loading, Let's Get Sort-of-Real

Source URL: https://www.dunnhumby.com/source-files/

Modules: M2, M3, M4, M6

Priority: core

Focus: Free retail datasets. The Complete Journey has two years of all-category transactions for 2,500 frequent-shopper households, with demographics and direct-marketing campaign history. Breakfast at the Frat has 156 weeks of store-week sales, prices and promotions for four categories. Carbo-Loading has household transactions in pasta, sauce, syrup and pancake mix. Let's Get Sort-of-Real is a large simulated set (4.3 GB full, with smaller samples).

Teaching Suggestion: Use The Complete Journey for campaign-response and CLV projects, and Breakfast at the Frat for M3 price/promotion regression and elasticity exercises.

Cautions: Direct downloads, with no registration requirement visible. The license is on a linked Terms and Conditions page that was not reviewed. A Kaggle mirror of The Complete Journey (ref frtgnn/dunnhumby-the-complete-journey, 847 MB, listed under ODbL) also exists. Separately, 84.51 released a different 'Complete Journey' (801 households, one year, about 1.47M transactions) as the pip-installable completejourney_py (MIT code, Parquet): https://github.com/cunningjames/completejourney_py . Its README describes that data as simulated and for educational use only, which makes it the easiest Colab option.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:movielens | MovieLens datasets (ml-latest-small, ml-32m)

Focus: Movie ratings. ml-latest-small has 100,836 ratings from 610 users on 9,742 movies (1 MB). ml-32m has 32M ratings from 200,948 users on 87,585 movies (239 MB, released May 2024).

Teaching Suggestion: Collaborative-filtering and recommender-evaluation lab in M7; ml-latest-small fits easily in Colab.

Cautions: The DOI is the dataset paper: Harper & Konstan (2015), ACM TiiS 5(4). The README calls ml-latest-small a changing development set that is not appropriate for reported research results; check the license conditions before redistributing. 32M page: https://grouplens.org/datasets/movielens/32m/

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:ctr-avazu-criteo | CTR prediction benchmarks: Avazu (Kaggle) and Criteo 1TB Click Logs

Source URL: https://www.kaggle.com/c/avazu-ctr-prediction

Modules: M7, M8

Priority: optional

Focus: Two standard ad click-through datasets. Avazu is the Kaggle competition to predict whether a mobile ad is clicked. Criteo 1TB Click Logs covers 24 days with 13 integer and 26 hashed categorical features and is a larger version of the Kaggle Display Advertising Challenge data.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor-prepared subsamples for M7 classification with high-cardinality categoricals (hashing, target encoding, calibration). Too large for raw student download.

Cautions: Criteo 1TB: https://ailab.criteo.com/download-criteo-1tb-click-logs-dataset/ ; Hugging Face mirror: https://huggingface.co/datasets/criteo/CriteoClickLogs ; Display Advertising Challenge: https://www.kaggle.com/c/criteo-display-ad-challenge . Avazu row counts and file sizes were not visible (page is JS-rendered).

Rights or Access: free-registration

### additional:mlogit-train-modecanada | Train and ModeCanada choice datasets (R package mlogit)

Source URL: https://cran.csiro.au/web/packages/mlogit/vignettes/c2.formula.data.html

Modules: M4

Priority: recommended

Focus: Train is a Dutch stated-preference survey: respondents chose between two train trips differing in price, time, number of changes and comfort (up to 16 tasks each, wide format). ModeCanada records mode choice among train, air, bus and car in the Ontario-Quebec corridor (long format; 2,779 situations with all four modes available).

Teaching Suggestion: Conjoint-style multinomial/mixed logit and willingness-to-pay exercises (Train mimics a two-alternative conjoint).

Cautions: Python option: xlogit (pip install xlogit; GPU-accelerated mixed logit, MNL, WTP space) uses an electricity-supplier choice dataset (electricity_long.csv) in its quick start: https://xlogit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ . AER datasets were not checked.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:statsmodels-rdatasets | statsmodels example datasets and Rdatasets (get_rdataset)

Source URL: https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/datasets/index.html

Modules: M1, M3, M4

Priority: recommended

Focus: statsmodels bundles 28 datasets (e.g. modechoice travel choice, grunfeld, fair, randhie), and sm.datasets.get_rdataset() pulls any of the 3,648 CRAN datasets in Rdatasets into pandas.

Teaching Suggestion: Zero-setup data for M3 regression drills in Colab. get_rdataset lets Python students use classic R textbook data without installing R.

Cautions: Rdatasets index: https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/Rdatasets/

Rights or Access: open

### additional:dominicks-finer-foods | Dominick's Finer Foods scanner data

Source URL: https://www.chicagobooth.edu/research/kilts/research-data/dominicks

Modules: M3, M6, M8

Priority: recommended

Focus: Weekly store-level UPC sales, price, profit margin and deal codes for 29 categories (3,500+ UPCs) from about 100 Chicago-area stores, 1989 to 1994, plus daily customer counts and store demographics. CSV, SAS and Stata.

Teaching Suggestion: Price-elasticity and promotion regressions in M3 using one category's movement file (e.g. soft drinks or cereals).

Cautions: Free direct download. The terms say 'for academic research purposes only' and do not address teaching; confirm classroom use with marketingdata@chicagobooth.edu. Source URL: https://github.com/facebookexperimental/Robyn

Modules: M6, M8

Modules: M4, M6, M8, AI

Priority: core

Focus: The MMM example notebook builds a synthetic dataset step by step (179 weeks, two channels, events, trend, adstock and saturation) and then recovers the parameters. The repo's data/ folder provides mmm_example.csv and cdnow_transactions.csv for the MMM and CLV quickstarts.

It warns about mistakes such as flat priors on saturation. The data/ folder contents are inferred from quickstart code because the listing was blocked.

### additional:reddit-data-access | Reddit Data API and Reddit for Researchers access rules

Source URL: https://support.reddithelp.com/hc/en-us/articles/14945211791892-Developer-Platform-Accessing-Reddit-Data

Modules: M5

Priority: recommended

Focus: Reddit's policy: the Data API is rate-limited and bulk export is restricted. Academic research must go through the Reddit for Researchers program, and content may not be used for model training without Reddit's consent.

Teaching Suggestion: Required policy reading for M5 social-media analysis. It explains why students should not scrape Reddit or use the API for research projects, and how research access works.

Cautions: Reddit for Researchers eligibility is not listed; applications go through a support ticket. Requests from hosted-service IP ranges, likely including cloud notebooks, need OAuth or a login.

Rights or Access: free-registration

### additional:bluesky-api-jetstream | Bluesky developer docs and Jetstream

Source URL: https://docs.bsky.app/

Modules: M5

Priority: recommended

Focus: Docs for the open AT Protocol HTTP API and SDKs (official TypeScript and Go; community Python and Dart). Jetstream is a lightweight JSON stream of public network events, filterable by collection or account.

Teaching Suggestion: The most practical open source of live social-media text for M5, via the Python SDK. Use Jetstream for prototypes; Bluesky says it is not the right tool for research-grade archives.

Cautions: Jetstream post: https://docs.bsky.app/blog/jetstream (public instances; events are not signed). Authentication and terms are not on the landing page; review Bluesky's developer guidelines and ethics/IRB considerations before collecting user posts.

Cautions: Springer page: https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-030-49720-0 (likely in UIUC's SpringerLink holdings; not checked). The chapter list was not verified; topics are expected to mirror the R edition (regression, segmentation, choice modeling).

### additional:github-pages-quickstart-plain-html | Quickstart for GitHub Pages

Source URL: https://docs.github.com/en/pages/quickstart

Modules: M1, M2, WIKI

Priority: core

Focus: Shortest path to a live site: create a username.github.io repo and publish from a branch. The default pipeline assumes Jekyll and a _config.yml.

Teaching Suggestion: Baseline for the plain HTML + JS option: commit hand-written pages or single-file interactive HTML artifacts, and add an empty .nojekyll file to skip Jekyll processing.

Cautions: The quickstart itself does not mention .nojekyll; that tip comes from Quarto's GitHub Pages guide. Plain HTML gives full control and needs no build step, but you get no built-in navigation, search, cross-references or notebook rendering. Pair it with Pagefind for search.

### additional:fader-hardie-lee-2005-rfm-clv-isovalue | RFM and CLV: Using Iso-Value Curves for Customer Base Analysis

### additional:pymc-marketing-clv-quickstart | PyMC-Marketing CLV Quickstart (BG/NBD + Gamma-Gamma) and CLV model notebooks

Source URL: https://www.pymc-marketing.io/en/stable/notebooks/clv/clv_quickstart.html

Modules: M2, M4

Priority: core

Focus: Uses CDNOW to build an RFM summary with clv.utils.rfm_summary and a train/test split, fits BG/NBD by MAP and MCMC, and computes P(alive) and expected purchases. It then checks the Gamma-Gamma independence assumption, fits Gamma-Gamma and computes discounted CLV with uncertainty intervals.

Teaching Suggestion: Main CLV lab notebook. Sibling notebooks cover Pareto/NBD, MBG/NBD, standalone Gamma-Gamma and sBG with cohorts and covariates for subscription settings.

Cautions: BG/NBD: https://www.pymc-marketing.io/en/stable/notebooks/clv/bg_nbd.html. Pareto/NBD: https://www.pymc-marketing.io/en/stable/notebooks/clv/pareto_nbd.html. Gamma-Gamma: https://www.pymc-marketing.io/en/stable/notebooks/clv/gamma_gamma.html. sBG: https://www.pymc-marketing.io/en/stable/notebooks/clv/sbg.html. The quickstart doesn't mention migrating from lifetimes. The rfm_summary definitions of frequency and recency differ from standard RFM scoring, which is worth flagging to students.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:acquisti-taylor-wagman-2016-economics-of-privacy | The Economics of Privacy

Source URL: https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/jel.54.2.442

Modules: M2, M8

Priority: recommended

Focus: Survey of theory and evidence on the value of protecting versus disclosing personal data. It concludes there is no unified theory, that privacy protection can raise or lower welfare, and that consumers often cannot see how their data is used.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor background and an optional reading that frames privacy as a trade-off rather than a compliance checklist.

### additional:statsmodels-robust-covariance | statsmodels OLSResults.get_robustcov_results: HC0-HC3, cluster, HAC and panel covariance options

Modules: M3

Focus: Reference for every cov_type in statsmodels: HC0-HC3, cluster (CRV1, with integer 'groups'), cluster-crv3, cluster-jk, HAC (maxlags), hac-groupsum (Driscoll-Kraay) and hac-panel.

### additional:pyfixest-docs-and-llm-skill | PyFixest: fast high-dimensional fixed-effects regression in Python (quickstart, tutorials, llms.txt and agent skill file)

Source URL: https://pyfixest.org/getting-started.html

Modules: AI, M3, M6

Priority: core

Focus: Python port of R's fixest. It offers feols, fepois, feglm and quantreg with multi-way fixed effects; iid, HC1-HC3, CRV1/CRV3, Newey-West and Driscoll-Kraay vcov; wild cluster bootstrap; DiD and event-study estimators; and etable regression tables. The docs site publishes llms.txt and a ready-made skill file meant to be saved as SKILL.md or Agent.md so LLM coding tools write correct PyFixest code.

Teaching Suggestion: Recommended regression package for the course. Have teams add the provided skill file (https://pyfixest.org/skills.llms.md) to their project repo before using Claude Code or Cursor, then require them to state and justify their vcov choice.

Cautions: Repo: https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest (MIT). The skill page lists vcov options but does not say what the defaults are. Check the API docs before telling students the defaults; fixest-style packages often cluster by the first fixed effect when FEs are present. HC2 and HC3 are not supported with FEs or IV.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:abadie-athey-imbens-wooldridge-clustering | When Should You Adjust Standard Errors for Clustering?

Source URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w24003

Modules: M3, M6

Priority: recommended

Focus: Argues that clustering is a design question. Clustered SEs are needed when sampling is two-stage or when treatment assignment is correlated within clusters, and the paper proposes less conservative estimators for intermediate cases.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor background for the 'at what level should I cluster?' slide. Also gives students a rule to apply when an AI tool clusters 'by everything'.

### additional:gelman-loken-forking-paths | The garden of forking paths: Why multiple comparisons can be a problem, even when there is no 'fishing expedition' or 'p-hacking' and the research hypothesis was posited ahead of time

Source URL: https://sites.stat.columbia.edu/gelman/research/unpublished/p_hacking.pdf

Modules: M3, M6, AI

Priority: recommended

Focus: Shows that data-dependent analysis choices (exclusions, codings, subgroups, interactions) invalidate p-values even without deliberate fishing. Remedies include preregistration, replication and multilevel modeling.

Teaching Suggestion: Framing reading for 'vibe coding' risks. AI agents make it nearly free to try dozens of specifications, so students should log every specification an AI tool ran and report all of them.

Cautions: The link redirects from stat.columbia.edu to sites.stat.columbia.edu; the final URL is used here.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:nau-log-log-elasticity-example | Regression example: log transformation and additional predictors (beer sales, own- and cross-price elasticities)

Source URL: https://people.duke.edu/~rnau/regex4.htm

Modules: M3

Priority: core

Focus: Business-school worked example. A log-log regression of 18-pack beer sales on price gives an own-price elasticity of about -6.7, and adding other carton sizes' prices yields cross-price elasticities. It also explains reading log-unit errors as percentages.

Teaching Suggestion: Interpretation reference for the log-log and elasticity lesson. Students reproduce the example in statsmodels or pyfixest with AI help and check that they get the same coefficients.

### additional:bijmolt-vanheerde-pieters-2005-price-elasticity | New Empirical Generalizations on the Determinants of Price Elasticity

Source URL: https://repository.tilburguniversity.edu/items/813834f9-4626-45f8-ad0a-2920a545e089

Modules: M3

Focus: Meta-analysis of published price elasticities and of what drives their size (category, data type, model specification, estimation method).

Teaching Suggestion: Benchmark for sanity-checking student estimates. If a regression returns a price elasticity of +0.3 or -15, that is a red flag.

### additional:korkames-stanley-stremersch-2026-ad-elasticity | Meta-Analysis of Advertising Effectiveness: New Insights from Improved Bias Corrections

Source URL: https://pure.eur.nl/en/publications/meta-analysis-of-advertising-effectiveness-new-insights-from-impr/

Modules: M3, M6

Priority: recommended

Focus: Meta-analysis of 538 B2C own-brand advertising elasticities. Modern publication-bias corrections cut the mean effect more than fivefold (short-term about 0.0008, long-term about 0.03), in line with RCT evidence, and internet advertising shows the highest elasticity.

Teaching Suggestion: Use it with a log-log sales response regression to discuss why observational ad elasticities run high (endogeneity and publication bias).

Cautions: The Erasmus repository offers the final PDF under the Dutch 'Article 25fa' (Taverne) provision. The classic benchmark is Sethuraman, Tellis & Briesch (2011): 872 estimates with a mean short-term elasticity of 0.12 (https://scholar.smu.edu/business_marketing_research/12; SSRN doi 10.2139/ssrn.1866002). Its repository title differs from the published JMR title 'How Well Does Advertising Work?'.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:shapiro-hitsch-tuchman-tv-advertising | TV Advertising Effectiveness and Profitability: Generalizable Results from 288 Brands

Source URL: https://papers.ssrn.com/abstract=3273476

Modules: M3, M6

Priority: recommended

Focus: Regression-based estimates of TV ad elasticities for 288 CPG brands. Elasticities are much smaller than prior literature, many are insignificant, and marginal ROI is negative for over 80% of brands.

Teaching Suggestion: Flagship case for 'advertising response as regression'. Students can read the Kellogg Insight summary (https://insight.kellogg.northwestern.edu/article/tv-advertising-is-usually-not-worth-it).

Cautions: Published in Econometrica (2021); the SSRN page does not name the journal. The study covers 288 brands. A related NBER paper, 'Generalizable and Robust TV Advertising Effects' (w27684), also exists.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:jin-2017-bayesian-mmm-carryover-shape | Bayesian Methods for Media Mix Modeling with Carryover and Shape Effects

Source URL: https://research.google/pubs/bayesian-methods-for-media-mix-modeling-with-carryover-and-shape-effects/

Modules: M3, M6

Priority: recommended

Focus: Foundational paper on modern MMM. A regression of sales on adstocked (carryover) and saturated (shape) media spend, estimated with Bayesian methods, showing that priors dominate in small samples and the optimal mix is highly uncertain.

### additional:pymc-marketing-mmm-log-log | PyMC-Marketing: Additive vs Log vs Log-Log MMMs (and the end-to-end MMM example)

Focus: Compares additive, log-link and log-log MMM specifications with adstock and saturation on synthetic weekly data. It explains when log-log channel coefficients can be read as elasticities and when they are semi-elasticities, then compares ROAS and budget plans against the known truth.

### additional:statqa-llms-good-statisticians | Are Large Language Models Good Statisticians?

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07815

Modules: M3, M6, AI

Priority: recommended

Focus: StatQA benchmark (11,623 examples) on choosing and applying hypothesis tests. GPT-4o reached only about 65%. LLMs mostly make applicability errors (using a method whose assumptions fail), whereas humans mostly confuse task types.

Teaching Suggestion: Supports a rule for the wiki: make the AI state each method's assumptions and check them on the data before trusting its test or regression.

Cautions: Possibly NeurIPS 2024 Datasets & Benchmarks track; this is from recollection, as the arXiv page lists no venue.

### additional:xlogit-mixed-logit-python | xlogit: GPU-accelerated multinomial and mixed logit estimation in Python

Source URL: https://github.com/arteagac/xlogit

Modules: M4

Priority: core

Focus: Estimates MNL, conditional logit and mixed logit (normal, lognormal, triangular, uniform and truncated-normal mixing), handles panel and unbalanced data with Halton draws, fits WTP-space models, and runs on GPU via CuPy when available.

Teaching Suggestion: Estimation engine for the CBC exercise. The WTP-space notebook (yogurt data ported from R logitr) shows WTP estimated directly, and a Colab-ready mixed logit notebook is provided.

Cautions: WTP-space notebook: https://xlogit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/notebooks/wtp_space.html. Colab: https://colab.research.google.com/github/arteagac/xlogit/blob/master/examples/mixed_logit_model.ipynb. An older alternative is pylogit (BSD-3, https://github.com/timothyb0912/pylogit), which covers MNL, nested and normal-mixing mixed logit and has notebooks in examples/; its maintenance status is unclear.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:biogeme-discrete-choice | Biogeme: maximum likelihood (and Bayesian) estimation of discrete choice models

Source URL: https://biogeme.epfl.ch/

Modules: M4

Priority: optional

Focus: Mature discrete choice estimation package built on pandas. Version 3.3.5 adds JAX-based evaluation, Bayesian estimation and richer diagnostics, alongside an examples gallery, a primer and YouTube tutorials.

Teaching Suggestion: Pointer for students who want nested or cross-nested logit or latent-class choice models beyond xlogit.

Cautions: Requires Python 3.12 or later (pip install biogeme). The site asks users to cite the Biogeme primer.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:choice-learn-artefact | Choice-Learn: discrete choice modeling with large datasets

### additional:pymc-marketing-customer-choice-mnl | PyMC-Marketing customer choice notebooks: Multinomial Logit and the IIA property (plus mixed logit, nested logit, MaxDiff)

Source URL: https://www.pymc-marketing.io/en/stable/notebooks/customer_choice/mnl_logit.html

Modules: M4

Priority: recommended

Focus: Bayesian MNL on heating-system choice data, with counterfactual market-share simulations: raising one product's price and removing a product. It shows IIA's proportional substitution and motivates nested logit. Sibling notebooks cover mixed logit, nested logit, consideration sets, MaxDiff and Bayesian BLP.

Teaching Suggestion: Market-simulator demo: change a price and watch shares move. It also gives a concrete, visible case of IIA's proportional-substitution problem.

Cautions: The MNL notebook does not compute WTP; add -beta_attribute/beta_price yourself. Mixed logit: https://www.pymc-marketing.io/en/stable/notebooks/customer_choice/mixed_logit.html. MaxDiff: https://www.pymc-marketing.io/en/stable/notebooks/customer_choice/maxdiff.html. A simpler PyMC gallery version on the same heating data: https://www.pymc.io/projects/examples/en/latest/generalized_linear_models/GLM-discrete-choice_models.html.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:cbctools-logitr-helveston | cbcTools and logitr: R packages for designing choice-based conjoint surveys and estimating preference- and WTP-space logit models

Source URL: https://jhelvy.github.io/cbcTools/

Modules: M4

Priority: recommended

Focus: cbcTools covers profile generation, priors, random and D-optimal design (labeled, no-choice and dominance-removed), checks for balance, overlap and D-error, simulated choices, and power analysis. logitr fits MNL and mixed logit in preference or WTP space and predicts shares.

Teaching Suggestion: The cleanest end-to-end CBC design workflow. Use it with R, or have students ask an AI assistant to reproduce a cbcTools design in Python and compare D-errors.

Cautions: logitr docs: https://jhelvy.github.io/logitr/. The DOI is for the logitr JSS article.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:pydoe-experimental-design | PyDOE: Design of Experiments for Python (successor to pyDOE3)

Source URL: https://github.com/pydoe/pydoe

Modules: M4, M6

Priority: optional

Focus: Python DOE toolkit covering full and fractional factorial, response-surface, space-filling (Latin hypercube, Sobol), optimal, Taguchi and sequential designs.

Teaching Suggestion: Generate full or fractional factorial profile sets for a toy conjoint. For real CBC choice-set designs, prefer cbcTools or a survey platform.

Cautions: pyDOE3 (https://github.com/relf/pyDOE3) is archived and its README tells users to migrate to pydoe/pydoe. pyDOE3 documented optimal designs (Fedorov, DETMAX; D, A and I criteria); confirm the same functions exist in PyDOE.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:sawtooth-lighthouse-studio | Sawtooth Software Lighthouse Studio (CBC, ACBC, MaxDiff, HB estimation, market simulator)

Focus: Industry-standard conjoint and MaxDiff platform with CBC, Adaptive CBC, HB estimation and a market simulator for product, price and competitor scenarios. A free starter account is available.

Teaching Suggestion: Industry reference point and demo. Its technical-papers library (CBC, HB, market simulators, design) is excellent free instructor background.

### additional:conjointly-academic-fee-waiver | Conjointly: conjoint analysis for students and academics (fee waiver)

Source URL: https://conjointly.com/faq/conjoint-analysis-for-students-and-academics/

Modules: M4

Priority: recommended

Focus: Online survey and conjoint platform. Its free Basic tier allows Generic Conjoint up to 20 responses. An academic fee waiver for students and teachers with an academic email gives a one-year licence with unlimited respondents, excluding panel sampling and paid services.

Teaching Suggestion: Easiest way for project teams to field a real CBC. Have students apply for waivers early, since processing can take up to 4 weeks.

Cautions: Free academic users generally get no support. The site lists an 'API and MCP' resource (https://conjointly.com/api/) that was not inspected. Pricing page: https://conjointly.com/pricing/.

### additional:green-srinivasan-1978-conjoint | Conjoint Analysis in Consumer Research: Issues and Outlook

### additional:rao-2014-applied-conjoint-analysis | Applied Conjoint Analysis

Source URL: https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-540-87753-0

Modules: M4

Priority: core

Focus: Comprehensive text in ten chapters: ratings-based and choice-based designs, part-worth estimation, many-attribute methods, and applications to product design, positioning, segmentation, pricing and other marketing-mix decisions.

Teaching Suggestion: Main textbook reference for the conjoint unit. Assign chapters through the UIUC library's Springer access.

### additional:hauser-rao-2004-conjoint-review | Conjoint Analysis, Related Modeling, and Applications

Source URL: https://mitsloan.mit.edu/shared/ods/documents/?PublicationDocumentID=5592

Modules: M4

Priority: core

Focus: Free review of the field's history, design choices, estimation methods (including HB and adaptive approaches) and applications.

Teaching Suggestion: Free assigned reading that complements Rao (2014).

Cautions: Download link taken from John Hauser's MIT 'Papers & Books' page.

### additional:toubia-hauser-simester-2004-polyhedral-cbc | Polyhedral Methods for Adaptive Choice-Based Conjoint Analysis

Source URL: https://mitsloan.mit.edu/shared/ods/documents/?PublicationDocumentID=4040

Modules: M4

Priority: optional

Focus: Adaptive question design for CBC that picks each next choice set to shrink the feasible region of part-worths as fast as possible. A key step from classic to optimization- and ML-based conjoint.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor background on adaptive design. It also motivates the idea that question design and estimation interact.

Cautions: Companion review: Toubia, Evgeniou & Hauser (2007), 'Optimization-Based and Machine-Learning Methods for Conjoint Analysis' (https://mitsloan.mit.edu/shared/ods/documents/?PublicationDocumentID=5582). See also Hauser, Eggers & Selove (2019, Marketing Science), 'The Strategic Implications of Scale in Choice-Based Conjoint Analysis' (https://mitsloan.mit.edu/shared/ods/documents/?PublicationDocumentID=5576). Toubia's recent conjoint-adjacent work on LLM digital twins appears below.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:allenby-brazell-howell-rossi-2014-economic-valuation | Economic Valuation of Product Features

Source URL: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11129-014-9150-x

Modules: M4

Priority: recommended

Focus: Values a product feature as the change in equilibrium profits, using a conjoint-estimated demand system plus competitor and cost data. With digital camera data, this gives very different answers from naive WTP or welfare measures.

Teaching Suggestion: Key reading for why the 'WTP = -beta/beta_price' shortcut can mislead. It motivates building market simulators with competitors.

Rights or Access: library

---

### additional:brand-israeli-ngwe-llms-market-research | Using LLMs for Market Research

Source URL: https://papers.ssrn.com/abstract=4395751

Modules: AI, M4, M6, M7, M8

Priority: core

Focus: Draws many GPT responses per survey question to estimate WTP for product features. Estimates are sometimes close to human studies but often inaccurate and occasionally wrong-signed. Fine-tuning on past surveys helps for new features in the same category but not for new categories or segment differences.

Teaching Suggestion: Anchor reading for an exercise in which teams run a synthetic-respondent conjoint with an LLM, compare it with their human CBC, and report where it diverges.

Cautions: The abstract became more cautious over revisions: the HBS page (https://www.hbs.edu/faculty/Pages/item.aspx?num=63859, July 2024) calls the WTP estimates 'plausible', while the April 2026 SSRN revision says they are often inaccurate. Assign the latest version.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:goli-singh-llms-capture-human-preferences | Frontiers: Can Large Language Models Capture Human Preferences?

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.02531

Modules: M4, AI

Priority: core

Focus: Asks GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 intertemporal-choice conjoint-style questions across languages. Both models are far less patient than humans, and 'chain-of-thought conjoint' narrows but doesn't close the gap. The authors recommend LLMs for generating hypotheses, not as stand-ins for respondents.

Teaching Suggestion: Paired reading with Brand et al. Good for a discussion of when synthetic respondents mislead.

Cautions: Published in Marketing Science (2024). The DOI could not be confirmed because INFORMS blocked automated access.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:arora-chakraborty-nishimura-2025-ai-human-hybrids | AI-Human Hybrids for Marketing Research: Leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) as Collaborators

Source URL: https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/00222429241276529

Modules: AI, M4, M5, M7, M8

Priority: core

Focus: Frames LLMs as collaborators in qualitative research (synthetic respondents, interviews, theme coding) and quantitative research (synthetic survey data). Few-shot prompting and RAG improve quality, and a study replication was run with a Fortune 500 food company.

Teaching Suggestion: Practitioner-facing JM framework for how to use LLMs in market research, rather than whether to. It fits the M4 synthetic-respondent activity.

Rights or Access: library

---

### additional:gui-toubia-llm-simulation-causal-inference | The Challenge of Using LLMs to Simulate Human Behavior: A Causal Inference Perspective

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.15524

Modules: AI, M4, M6, M7, M8

Priority: core

Focus: Shows that LLM-simulated price and attribute experiments are confounded: changing the treatment in a prompt shifts unstated factors, which produces implausible demand curves in a 40-product study. Proposes 'unblinding' (revealing the design) and fine-tuning as fixes.

Teaching Suggestion: Required reading before any synthetic conjoint or pricing exercise. It explains why naive prompts give wrong elasticities.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:twin-2k-500-digital-twins-dataset | Twin-2K-500: A dataset for building digital twins of over 2,000 people based on their answers to over 500 questions

Source URL: https://huggingface.co/datasets/LLM-Digital-Twin/Twin-2K-500

Modules: M4, M8, AI

Priority: optional

Focus: Four-wave survey of 2,058 US participants (demographics, psychological scales, economic preferences, behavioral-economics experiments, and a pricing survey per the paper) with a test-retest wave, released for building and testing LLM persona simulations.

Teaching Suggestion: Optional project dataset for teams testing whether LLM 'twins' reproduce individual consumer answers.

Cautions: 733 MB of Parquet on Hugging Face, so link to it rather than mirroring. The HF card does not mention the pricing survey; the arXiv abstract does.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:digital-twins-funhouse-mirrors | Digital Twins as Funhouse Mirrors: Five Key Distortions

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.19088

Modules: M4, M8, AI

Priority: core

Focus: Mega-study of 19 preregistered studies and 164 outcomes. Digital twins built from 500+ answers per person beat a generic LLM only slightly and correlate weakly with real answers (mean r = 0.20). Five distortions are documented: insufficient individuation, stereotyping, representation bias, ideological bias and hyper-rationality.

Teaching Suggestion: The most current large-scale validation (2025-26) of synthetic respondents. Use it as the critical counterweight in the synthetic-conjoint activity.

Cautions: A more optimistic 2025 counterpoint is Maier et al., 'LLMs Reproduce Human Purchase Intent via Semantic Similarity Elicitation of Likert Ratings' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08338). Its free-text-plus-embedding method reached about 90% of human test-retest reliability on 57 personal-care surveys. Some of its authors work in industry (Wiecki is, from recollection, at PyMC Labs).

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:bisbee-2024-synthetic-replacements-perils | Synthetic Replacements for Human Survey Data? The Perils of Large Language Models

Source URL: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/political-analysis/article/synthetic-replacements-for-human-survey-data-the-perils-of-large-language-models/B92267DC26195C7F36E63EA04A47D2FE

Modules: M4, M8, AI

Priority: recommended

Focus: ChatGPT personas match ANES group averages but show too little variance, yield regression coefficients that differ significantly from the survey's, shift with small prompt changes, and drift over three months.

Teaching Suggestion: Open-access critique showing that synthetic samples can get the means right but the regressions wrong, which ties M3 back to M4.

Cautions: Optimistic counterpart: Argyle et al. (2023), 'Out of One, Many: Using Language Models to Simulate Human Samples', Political Analysis 31(3), 337-351, doi 10.1017/pan.2023.2 (paywalled). Also Horton, Filippas & Manning, 'Homo Silicus', NBER w31122 (https://www.nber.org/papers/w31122).

Rights or Access: open

### additional:sklearn-clustering-and-gmm | scikit-learn User Guide: Clustering, and Gaussian Mixture Models

Source URL: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/clustering.html

Modules: M4, M7

Priority: core

Focus: Reference for KMeans and MiniBatchKMeans, agglomerative clustering (Ward, complete, average, single), spectral clustering, DBSCAN and HDBSCAN, OPTICS and BIRCH, with a comparison table and evaluation metrics. The mixture chapter covers GaussianMixture, BIC-based selection of k and BayesianGaussianMixture.

Teaching Suggestion: Primary API reference for the segmentation lab. The BIC model-selection example answers the 'how many segments?' question.

Cautions: GMM page: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/mixture.html. The KMeans section links a silhouette-analysis example for choosing k.

Rights or Access: open

Source URL: https://github.com/Labo-Lacourse/stepmix

Source URL: https://doi.org/10.1177/0022242919873106

### additional:humphreys-wang-2018-automated-text-analysis | Automated Text Analysis for Consumer Research

Source URL: https://doi.org/10.1093/jcr/ucx104

Modules: M5

Priority: recommended

Focus: A step-by-step methodological guide to dictionary-based and other automated text analysis for consumer research: building constructs, operationalizing them, and checking validity.

Teaching Suggestion: Background reading on construct validity for dictionary methods. Its stages (question, data, construct, operationalization, validation) can be reused as a checklist for team projects.

### additional:hartmann-2019-comparing-text-classification | Comparing automated text classification methods

Source URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijresmar.2018.09.009

Modules: M5, M7

Priority: recommended

Focus: Benchmarks lexicon methods against machine-learning classifiers (random forests, SVM, naive Bayes, neural nets and others) across dozens of social media and review datasets, and gives guidance on which to use when.

Teaching Suggestion: Reading behind a 'dictionary vs. ML classifier' in-class comparison. Students can rerun a mini version with scikit-learn on Yelp or Amazon reviews.

Cautions: Pre-LLM benchmark. Pair it with Hartmann et al. (2023) and Krugmann & Hartmann (2024) to show how the ranking of methods changed.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:hartmann-2023-more-than-a-feeling | More than a Feeling: Accuracy and Application of Sentiment Analysis

Source URL: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167811622000477

Modules: M5, M7

Priority: core

Focus: Shows that sentiment-method accuracy varies widely and that inaccurate sentiment scores can bias downstream marketing conclusions. Transfer learning (fine-tuned RoBERTa) performs best, and the authors release SiEBERT, a ready-to-use model.

Teaching Suggestion: Core reading for sentiment. The released SiEBERT model fits in a 3-line Colab demo, so students can compare it with VADER on the same reviews.

Cautions: Model card: https://huggingface.co/siebert/sentiment-roberta-large-english (binary pos/neg; trained/evaluated on 15 datasets; license not stated on card). Usage: pipeline('sentiment-analysis', model='siebert/sentiment-roberta-large-english'). ScienceDirect blocked fetching, so the article's open-access status is unverified. Metadata confirmed on IDEAS and Univ. Hamburg page.

Rights or Access: library

### additional:netzer-2012-mine-your-own-business | Mine Your Own Business: Market-Structure Surveillance Through Text Mining

Source URL: https://doi.org/10.1287/mksc.1120.0713

Modules: M5, M4

Priority: recommended

Focus: Mines forum posts for brand co-mentions to build perceptual and market-structure maps, then compares them with survey and sales-based maps.

Teaching Suggestion: Case example linking text to M4 perceptual mapping. Students can replicate a simple brand co-occurrence network from Reddit or review text.

Cautions: Metadata from IDEAS/RePEc. A natural bridge to the network-analysis part of M5 (co-mention networks).

Rights or Access: library

### additional:tirunillai-tellis-2014-lda-online-chatter | Mining Marketing Meaning from Online Chatter: Strategic Brand Analysis of Big Data Using Latent Dirichlet Allocation

Source URL: https://doi.org/10.1509/jmr.12.0106

Modules: M5

Priority: recommended

Focus: Applies LDA to product reviews to extract quality dimensions and their valence, and tracks brand positions on those dimensions over time.

Teaching Suggestion: Anchor reading for the topic-modeling lesson. Students run gensim LDA or BERTopic on Amazon Reviews 2023 and compare their output with the paper's quality dimensions.

Cautions: DOI metadata confirmed via Crossref.

### additional:timoshenko-hauser-2019-customer-needs-ugc | Identifying Customer Needs from User-Generated Content

Source URL: https://doi.org/10.1287/mksc.2018.1123

Modules: M5, M7

Priority: recommended

Focus: Uses a CNN to filter non-informative review sentences and embeddings to cluster the rest, so human analysts can find customer needs in Amazon reviews more efficiently. UGC proves at least as rich a source of needs as interviews.

Teaching Suggestion: Case example on human-machine workflows. A natural team-project template: filter reviews with embeddings or an LLM, then have humans code needs.

Cautions: Plain-language summary for students: https://insight.kellogg.northwestern.edu/article/how-companies-can-mine-online-reviews-for-product-development-gold (seen in search). An updated LLM version of this workflow would make a good team project.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:gentzkow-kelly-taddy-2019-text-as-data | Text as Data

Source URL: https://doi.org/10.1257/jel.20181020

Modules: M5

Priority: optional

Focus: Economics survey of representing text numerically (document-term matrices), dictionary methods, penalized regression, topic models and word embeddings, with applications.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor-only background for the 'text to numbers' lecture. Optional reading for students who want more depth.

Cautions: DOI metadata confirmed via Crossref. Predates LLMs. For a more recent econ survey see Ash & Hansen (2023), 'Text Algorithms in Economics', Annual Review of Economics 15:659-688, doi 10.1146/annurev-economics-082222-074352 (Crossref-verified).

Rights or Access: library

### additional:krugmann-hartmann-2024-sentiment-genai | Sentiment Analysis in the Age of Generative AI

Source URL: https://link.springer.com/doi/10.1007/s40547-024-00143-4

Modules: M5, AI

Priority: core

Focus: Compares zero-shot GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and Llama 2 with established transfer-learning sentiment models on marketing text. The LLMs often match or beat them, accuracy depends on data source and text features, and Llama 2 gives the most useful explanations.

Teaching Suggestion: Core, accessible reading for the 'LLM as sentiment classifier' lab. Students replicate a mini version (VADER vs. SiEBERT vs. an LLM API) on 200 hand-labeled reviews.

Cautions: Open access; authors hold copyright.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:li-castelo-katona-sarvary-2024-llm-perceptual | Frontiers: Determining the Validity of Large Language Models for Automated Perceptual Analysis

Source URL: https://doi.org/10.1287/mksc.2023.0454

Modules: AI, M4, M5, M7

Priority: core

Focus: Tests whether LLM responses can stand in for survey respondents in perceptual mapping. LLM-based brand similarity and attribute ratings agree with human data over 75% of the time.

Teaching Suggestion: Bridge between M4 (perceptual maps) and M5: students ask an LLM for brand-similarity judgments and compare the result with a map built from review co-mentions.

Cautions: Metadata from IDEAS/RePEc. INFORMS press release: https://www.informs.org/News-Room/INFORMS-Releases/News-Releases/Can-Large-Language-Models-Replace-Human-Participants-in-Some-Future-Market-Research (seen in search).

Rights or Access: library

---

### additional:overgoor-knight-bart-2025-llm-annotated-regressors | Correcting Toward the Wrong Target: LLM-Annotated Regressors Under Noisy Human Benchmarks

Source URL: https://scholar.smu.edu/business_marketing_research/63

Modules: M5, M3, AI

Priority: optional

Focus: Argues that validating LLM labels against noisy human labels can mislead, because corrections pull estimates toward an attenuated target. Uses about 10k TV ads and proposes a diagnostic plus an IV estimator that uses a second human rater.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor background and an advanced reading that links M3 measurement error to LLM labeling. Shows why human 'gold' labels are not automatically gold.

Cautions: Working paper (Sept 2025); journal publication not confirmed.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:cheng-mayya-sedoc-silicon-llm-annotation | To Err Is Human; To Annotate, SILICON? Toward Robust Reproducibility in LLM Annotation

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14461

Modules: M5, AI

Priority: recommended

Focus: Shows how LLM-based annotation becomes irreproducible when proprietary models are retired, and proposes the SILICON workflow: decompose measurement error, choose open-weight backup models, and route low-confidence labels to auxiliary models.

Teaching Suggestion: Reading for the 'non-reproducibility' failure mode. Supports a course rule that teams log the model version, prompt, temperature and date, and keep an open-weight fallback.

Cautions: Preprint by business-school (NYU Stern) authors; no journal ref listed.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:gilardi-2023-chatgpt-outperforms-crowd-workers | ChatGPT outperforms crowd workers for text-annotation tasks

Source URL: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2305016120

Modules: M5, AI

Priority: core

Focus: On 2,382 tweets, zero-shot ChatGPT beat MTurk crowd workers on four of five annotation tasks, had higher intercoder agreement than crowd workers and trained annotators, and cost under a third of a cent per annotation (about 20 times cheaper).

Teaching Suggestion: Short core reading that motivates LLM labeling. Pair it with Reiss (2023) and Baumann et al. (2025) for the cautionary side.

Cautions: DOI and license confirmed via Crossref. arXiv version: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.15056. Results are for ChatGPT as of early 2023, so newer models differ.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:ludwig-mullainathan-rambachan-llm-econometric-framework | Large Language Models: An Applied Econometric Framework

Source URL: https://nber.org/papers/w33344

Modules: M5, M3, AI

Priority: recommended

Focus: Distinguishes prediction uses of LLMs, which need no training leakage, from estimation or measurement uses. For measurement, valid inference requires a small validation sample, because otherwise arbitrary choices such as the model or prompt can change results a lot.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor anchor for the module's validation rule: every LLM-coded variable needs a human-labeled validation subsample. Assign a simplified slide version to students.

Cautions: The NBER page is open. Was presented at the NBER SI 2026 ML session (conference PDF seen in search).

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:feuerriegel-2025-nlp-behavioural-science | Using natural language processing to analyse text data in behavioural science

Source URL: https://www.nature.com/articles/s44159-024-00392-z

Modules: M5, AI

Priority: core

Focus: Review of the NLP pipeline for behavioral research, from dictionaries through supervised ML to LLMs. Discusses interpretability versus accuracy and gives recommendations for rigor and reproducibility.

Teaching Suggestion: Core modern overview reading that updates Berger et al. (2020) for the LLM era. Its pipeline figure can serve as the M5 roadmap.

Cautions: Published online 4 Feb 2025; volume and pages not verified. Co-authors include marketing scholars Hartmann and Netzer. The open-access PDF is on the Columbia Business School site (seen in search).

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:tornberg-2024-best-practices-llm-annotation | Best Practices for Text Annotation with Large Language Models

Source URL: https://sociologica.unibo.it/article/view/19461

Modules: M5, AI

Priority: core

Focus: Practical guidelines for LLM-based text annotation: model choice, prompt design and iteration, stability testing, validation against human labels, transparency, and ethics.

Teaching Suggestion: Basis for an 'LLM annotation checklist' callout on the wiki and for the grading rubric of LLM-coded variables in team projects.

Cautions: Openly licensed, so short excerpts can be quoted on the wiki with attribution.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:egami-2023-design-based-supervised-learning | Using Imperfect Surrogates for Downstream Inference: Design-based Supervised Learning for Social Science Applications of Large Language Models

Source URL: https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/hash/d862f7f5445255090de13b825b880d59-Abstract.html

Modules: M5, M3, AI

Priority: optional

Focus: Shows that plugging LLM labels straight into regressions can bias estimates and confidence intervals even at 80-90% accuracy. Proposes DSL, a doubly robust estimator that combines surrogate labels with a random gold-standard subsample.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor background and an advanced optional reading on why and how to correct regressions that use LLM-coded variables.

Cautions: Related: Angelopoulos et al. (2023), 'Prediction-powered inference', Science 382(6671):669-674, doi 10.1126/science.adi6000 (Crossref-verified). The authors' DSL software was not verified here.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:reiss-2023-chatgpt-reliability-cautionary | Testing the Reliability of ChatGPT for Text Annotation and Classification: A Cautionary Remark

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.11085

Modules: M5, AI

Priority: recommended

Focus: Repeated runs and small prompt or setting changes produce inconsistent ChatGPT classifications, so unsupervised use without validation against human labels is not advisable.

Teaching Suggestion: Motivates an in-class exercise: rerun the same LLM classification with 3 prompt wordings and 2 temperatures and measure agreement (Krippendorff's alpha).

Cautions: See also Atreja et al. (2024), 'Prompt Design Matters for Computational Social Science Tasks but in Unpredictable Ways', https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11980 (likely ICWSM 2025; fetched), and Pangakis et al. (2023), 'Automated Annotation with Generative AI Requires Validation', https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00176 (fetched).

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:baumann-2025-llm-hacking | Large Language Model Hacking: Quantifying the Hidden Risks of Using LLMs for Text Annotation

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08825v2

Modules: M5, M6, AI

Priority: recommended

Focus: Across many replicated hypotheses, about 31% of tests using state-of-the-art LLM annotations reached incorrect conclusions, and the risk is highest near significance thresholds. Human annotations were the best safeguard of the 21 mitigations tested.

Teaching Suggestion: Key cautionary reading. It links naturally to M6 on p-hacking: changing models or prompts until results look significant is a form of p-hacking.

Cautions: Preprint (v2, Oct 2025); no journal ref yet.

Rights or Access: open

Source URL: https://www.nltk.org/book/

Modules: M5, M1

Priority: recommended

Focus: The free online NLTK book: tokenization, corpora, word frequencies, tagging, text classification and more, in 12 chapters.

Teaching Suggestion: Reference reading for the preprocessing lesson (chapters 1-3). Link specific sections rather than assigning the whole book.

Cautions: The original O'Reilly edition is from 2009 and the online edition was updated for Python 3. Some content is dated, but it remains the canonical NLTK reference. NLTK also bundles VADER (nltk.sentiment.vader).

### additional:vader-sentiment | VADER: A Parsimonious Rule-Based Model for Sentiment Analysis of Social Media Text (vaderSentiment)

Source URL: https://github.com/cjhutto/vaderSentiment

Modules: M5

Priority: core

Focus: Lexicon- and rule-based sentiment scorer tuned for social media. It handles negation, intensifiers, punctuation, capitalization, emoticons and slang, and returns compound and pos/neu/neg scores.

Teaching Suggestion: First hands-on sentiment demo in Colab (pip install vaderSentiment). Serves as the baseline that transformer and LLM classifiers are compared against.

Cautions: The paper DOI was confirmed via Crossref. The repo includes the lexicon and the evaluation datasets.

Teaching Suggestion: Code reference for the network lab: build a retweet or reply network from Bluesky, or a brand co-mention network from reviews, then compute degree and betweenness centrality.

Cautions: Community notebooks at NX-Guides, https://networkx.org/nx-guides/ (fetched), include a 'Facebook network analysis' exploratory notebook (Binder-ready) suitable as a ready-made in-class exercise. NetworkX is BSD-licensed per general knowledge; the license was not stated on the fetched page.

Rights or Access: open

Modules: M5

### additional:hinz-2011-seeding-strategies | Seeding Strategies for Viral Marketing: An Empirical Comparison

Source URL: https://doi.org/10.1509/jm.10.0088

Modules: M5, M6

Priority: core

Focus: Compares seeding strategies (high-degree hubs, bridges, random) with field experiments and real referral data. Seeding well-connected people can far outperform random seeding.

Teaching Suggestion: Core marketing reading for the network subsection. Students simulate hub vs. random seeding on a SNAP network in NetworkX and compare reach.

Cautions: DOI metadata confirmed via Crossref; summary is from general knowledge of the paper. Related: Goldenberg, Han, Lehmann & Hong (2009), 'The Role of Hubs in the Adoption Process', JM 73(2):1-13, doi 10.1509/jmkg.73.2.1; Trusov, Bucklin & Pauwels (2009), 'Effects of WOM versus Traditional Marketing', JM 73(5):90-102, doi 10.1509/jmkg.73.5.90; Katona, Zubcsek & Sarvary (2011), JMR 48(3):425-443, doi 10.1509/jmkr.48.3.425. All Crossref-verified.

### additional:aral-walker-2012-influential-susceptible | Identifying Influential and Susceptible Members of Social Networks

Source URL: https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1215842

Modules: M5, M6

Focus: Randomized experiment on Facebook (product adoption via an app) estimating who is influential and who is susceptible to influence, by demographics.

### additional:claude-cookbook-classification | Classification with Claude: Insurance Support Ticket Classifier (Claude Cookbook)

Source URL: https://platform.claude.com/cookbook/capabilities-classification-guide

Modules: M5, AI

Priority: core

Focus: Worked notebook comparing simple prompting (74%), retrieval of similar labeled examples (94%) and retrieval plus chain of thought (97%) on a 10-category text classifier. Includes a scikit-learn classification report and confusion matrix, and Promptfoo tests across temperatures.

Teaching Suggestion: Template for the M5 'LLM classifier' lab. Students swap in their own label set (e.g., complaint types in reviews), keep the evaluation harness, and report accuracy against human labels.

### additional:openai-batch-api | OpenAI Batch API guide

Source URL: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/batch

Modules: M5, AI

Priority: recommended

Focus: Asynchronous bulk requests at 50% lower cost with a 24-hour completion window. Input is a JSONL file (up to 50,000 requests, 200 MB) with custom_id for matching outputs, and it uses a separate rate-limit pool.

Teaching Suggestion: Reference for scaling a validated prompt from 200 to 50,000 reviews cheaply. Teach the pattern: pilot synchronously, validate, then batch.

Cautions: platform.openai.com/docs/guides/batch now redirects here. Output order may differ from input, so match on custom_id. Output files are deleted after 30 days.

### additional:kohavi-deng-vermeer-intuition-busters | A/B Testing Intuition Busters: Common Misunderstandings in Online Controlled Experiments

### additional:deng-2013-cuped | Improving the Sensitivity of Online Controlled Experiments by Utilizing Pre-Experiment Data (CUPED)

Source URL: https://exp-platform.com/cuped/

Modules: M6, M3

Priority: core

Focus: The original CUPED paper, which reduces A/B test variance by regressing out pre-experiment covariates. It is now standard on most experimentation platforms.

Teaching Suggestion: Pair with a Colab exercise in which students implement CUPED as OLS with a pre-period covariate and compare confidence-interval widths, linking back to M3 regression.

Cautions: The page links a free PDF at exp-platform.com/Documents/2013-02-CUPED-ImprovingSensitivityOfControlledExperiments.pdf

Rights or Access: open

### additional:ms-exp-deep-dive-variance-reduction | Deep Dive Into Variance Reduction

Source URL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/articles/deep-dive-into-variance-reduction/

Modules: M6

Priority: recommended

Focus: Explains CUPED as a regression adjustment that leaves the estimator consistent, shows its equivalence to Lin's ANCOVA estimator, and introduces the 'effective traffic multiplier' 1/(1-R^2) with real Microsoft numbers.

Teaching Suggestion: A readable companion to the CUPED paper. The traffic-multiplier idea makes a good short quiz question.

Cautions: The ExP articles index (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/group/experimentation-platform-exp/articles/) also has 'A/B Interactions: A Call to Relax' (2023) and pieces on experimenting with GenAI features.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:srm-taxonomy-kdd2019 | Diagnosing Sample Ratio Mismatch in Online Controlled Experiments: A Taxonomy and Rules of Thumb for Practitioners

Source URL: https://exp-platform.com/Documents/2019_KDDFabijanGupchupFuptaOmhoverVermeerDmitriev.pdf

Modules: M6

Priority: core

Focus: Defines SRM (observed group sizes deviate from the designed split), shows how often it invalidates results, and gives a taxonomy of causes across assignment, execution, logging, analysis and interference.

Teaching Suggestion: Use with a Colab chi-square SRM check. Lukas Vermeer's SRM Checker site (https://lukasvermeer.nl/srm/) has a manual checker, a FAQ and the cause taxonomy.

Cautions: The full author list isn't shown in what I fetched; the abbreviated list follows the PDF filename. The SRM Checker Chrome extension has been retired, but the website, docs and manual check remain (MIT-licensed repo).

Rights or Access: open

### additional:spotify-did-significance | How to Accurately Test Significance with Difference in Difference Models

### additional:blake-nosko-tadelis-2015 | Consumer Heterogeneity and Paid Search Effectiveness: A Large-Scale Field Experiment

### additional:lewis-rao-2015-qje | The Unfavorable Economics of Measuring the Returns to Advertising

Source URL: https://ideas.repec.org/a/oup/qjecon/v130y2015i4p1941-1973.html

Modules: M6, M8

Priority: core

Focus: Using a large set of field experiments, shows that individual-level sales are so noisy relative to ad effects that even huge experiments are badly underpowered to measure ad ROI.

Teaching Suggestion: Pair with the power calculators. Students compute the sample size needed to detect a realistic ad lift and see the 'unfavorable economics' for themselves.

Cautions: The oa_url is an earlier AEA 2014 conference draft found in search, not the published version.

### additional:gordon-zettelmeyer-2019-facebook | A Comparison of Approaches to Advertising Measurement: Evidence from Big Field Experiments at Facebook

Source URL: https://www.kellogg.northwestern.edu/academics-research/research/detail/2019/a-comparison-of-approaches-to-advertising-measurement-evidence-from/

Modules: M6, M8

Priority: core

Focus: Benchmarks matching, regression adjustment and propensity-score methods against large Facebook RCTs. Observational methods often miss the experimental lift by large margins.

Teaching Suggestion: Assigned anchor. Students try to recover an RCT effect with observational methods on a dataset like Hillstrom and reflect on why it fails.

Cautions: A non-technical Kellogg/Facebook white paper is also available: https://www.kellogg.northwestern.edu/faculty/gordon_b/files/kellogg_fb_whitepaper.pdf

### additional:gordon-moakler-zettelmeyer-2023-close-enough | Close Enough? A Large-Scale Exploration of Non-Experimental Approaches to Advertising Measurement

Source URL: https://www.kellogg.northwestern.edu/academics-research/research/detail/2023/close-enough-a-large-scale-exploration-of-non-experimental/

Modules: M6, M8

Priority: recommended

Focus: Uses a large set of Facebook RCTs to test whether double/debiased ML and rich user-level data let observational methods recover experimental ad effects. Mostly they don't, even with rich data.

Teaching Suggestion: Follow-up to Gordon et al. (2019) that shows ML doesn't solve confounding. Good for a debate on 'can AI replace experiments?'.

Cautions: Volume and issue not verified. Check the exact number of experiments against the abstract before quoting.

### additional:johnson-lewis-nubbemeyer-ghost-ads | Ghost Ads: Improving the Economics of Measuring Online Ad Effectiveness

Source URL: https://www.kellogg.northwestern.edu/faculty/research/detail/2017/ghost-ads-improving-the-economics-of-measuring-online-ad

Modules: M6, M8

Priority: recommended

Focus: Introduces 'ghost ads', which log the ads control users would have seen, to build an exposed-vs-would-have-been-exposed comparison. It is cheaper and more precise than PSA or intent-to-treat ad experiments.

Teaching Suggestion: Explains how platform lift studies (Meta/Google conversion lift) actually work, and links ITT vs. treatment-on-treated to the IV material.

Cautions: I didn't see a DOI. Won the 2022 AMA Weitz-Winer-O'Dell award, per AMA search results.

Rights or Access: free-registration

### additional:csdid-python | csdid: Callaway and Sant'Anna difference-in-differences for Python

Modules: M6

Priority: recommended

Focus: A Python port of R's did package. It estimates group-time ATT(g,t) under staggered adoption (with doubly robust options) and aggregates to event-study, calendar or group effects, with plots.

Teaching Suggestion: Staggered-adoption lab on the mpdta minimum-wage example in the README. Students compare its results with naive TWFE from pyfixest.

Cautions: Needs the drdid library installed separately from GitHub. Docs: d2cml-ai.github.io/csdid/. No year given.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:differences-python | differences: difference-in-differences estimation and inference for Python

Source URL: https://github.com/bernardodionisi/differences

Modules: M6

Priority: optional

Focus: Implements Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021) ATT(g,t) through an ATTgt class, plus Sant'Anna and Zhao (2020) DR-DiD, multi-valued treatments and triple differences.

Teaching Suggestion: An alternative to csdid for students who want a richer API. Use for cross-checking estimates.

Cautions: Docs: https://bernardodionisi.github.io/differences/latest/ . The repo has few commits (58), so recent maintenance is unclear.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:pysyncon | pysyncon: a Python module for the synthetic control method

Source URL: https://github.com/sdfordham/pysyncon

Modules: M6

Priority: core

Focus: Implements classic, robust, augmented and penalized synthetic control with placebo tests and confidence intervals. Example notebooks reproduce Basque, Texas (from the Mixtape) and German reunification.

Teaching Suggestion: Synthetic control lab. Start from the Mixtape Texas notebook, then apply it to a brand or market-level marketing intervention.

Cautions: No year given.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:sparsesc-microsoft | SparseSC: Fit sparse synthetic control models in Python

Source URL: https://github.com/microsoft/SparseSC

Modules: M6

Priority: optional

Focus: An ML-enhanced synthetic control that penalizes feature and unit weights. It is useful when there are many donor units or many predictors.

Teaching Suggestion: Optional advanced alternative for project teams with many control markets.

Cautions: Docs: https://sparsesc.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ . Last commit date unclear and the repo is modestly active (about 90 stars). Background: Quistorff, Goldman and Thorpe (2020). No year given.

### additional:causalpy-pymc-labs | CausalPy: causal inference for quasi-experiments in Python

Source URL: https://github.com/pymc-labs/CausalPy

Modules: M6, AI

Priority: core

Focus: One API (Bayesian via PyMC, or scikit-learn) for synthetic control, GeoLift, DiD, staggered DiD, RDD, regression kink, interrupted time series, IV and IPW. It ships agent skills that teach AI coding assistants to use it.

Teaching Suggestion: The one-stop quasi-experiment toolkit for the wiki. Students can try its bundled AI-assistant skills (in Claude Code or Cursor) and critique the analyses they produce.

Cautions: Docs: https://causalpy.readthedocs.io . Per the docs, the skills live in causalpy/skills/ and are distributed through Decision AI Hub (hub.decision.ai). Year approximate.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:rdrobust-python | rdrobust: robust bias-corrected inference for regression discontinuity (Python)

Source URL: https://github.com/rdpackages/rdrobust

Modules: M6

Priority: recommended

Teaching Suggestion: RDD lab, e.g. loyalty-tier thresholds or rating cutoffs. Compare an AI-written 'OLS with a cutoff dummy' against rdrobust.

Cautions: PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/rdrobust/ (v2.1.1, released 2026-10-07, GPL-3.0-only). The old rdpackages.github.io/rdrobust page now just says the project moved to GitHub.

### additional:tfp-causalimpact | TFP CausalImpact: Python port of Google's CausalImpact

Focus: A Python/TensorFlow Probability implementation of CausalImpact. It estimates the effect of a marketing intervention on a time series against a Bayesian structural time-series counterfactual built from control series.

Cautions: Quick start is docs/quickstart.ipynb. Marked 'not an officially supported Google product'. The original R package (Apache-2.0) is at https://github.com/google/CausalImpact, with docs at https://google.github.io/CausalImpact/CausalImpact.html; its README points Python users to tfp-causalimpact. No year given.

### additional:pymc-marketing | PyMC-Marketing: Bayesian MMM, CLV and choice models in Python

Source URL: https://www.pymc-marketing.io/en/stable/

Modules: AI, M4, M6, M8

Priority: core

Focus: A Python Bayesian MMM with adstock/saturation, a DAG-based causal identification guide, lift-test and ROAS calibration and budget optimization, plus CLV/BTYD models that also tie into M4.

Teaching Suggestion: Main Python MMM. Assign the notebook 'Mitigating Unobserved Confounders in MMMs with Lift Test Likelihoods' (https://www.pymc-marketing.io/en/stable/notebooks/mmm/mmm_roas.html), where an omitted confounder flips the channel ROAS ranking and lift tests fix it.

Cautions: AI angle: the README links MMM-GPT (https://mmm-gpt.com/), an AI assistant for marketing analytics built on PyMC-Marketing. The repo also contains skills/mmm-modeling, .claude and .cursor directories, but GitHub blocked fetching them, so their contents are unverified. Lift-test integration notebook: https://www.pymc-marketing.io/en/stable/notebooks/mmm/mmm_lift_test.html . Requires Python >= 3.12.
