### additional:hillstrom-email-dataset | MineThatData E-Mail Analytics and Data Mining Challenge (Hillstrom dataset)

Source URL: https://blog.minethatdata.com/2008/03/minethatdata-e-mail-analytics-and-data.html

Modules: M6, M7, M4

Priority: core

Focus: 64,000 customers randomized to a men's email, a women's email or no email, with two-week visit, conversion and spend outcomes plus recency, history and channel covariates.

Teaching Suggestion: Workhorse dataset for M6: A/B analysis, CUPED-style adjustment, power, heterogeneous effects and uplift targeting. It is about 5 MB and easy to load in Colab.

Cautions: The blog post links a direct CSV. scikit-uplift loads it with fetch_hillstrom() (https://www.uplift-modeling.com/en/latest/api/datasets/fetch_hillstrom.html). No explicit license; it was released publicly for the 2008 challenge.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:ascarza-2018-retention-futility | Retention Futility: Targeting High-Risk Customers Might Be Ineffective

Source URL: https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1509/jmr.16.0163

Modules: M4, M6, M7

Priority: core

Focus: Field experiments show that targeting customers with the highest churn risk is not the same as targeting those most responsive to a retention offer. Uplift-based targeting beats risk-based targeting.

Teaching Suggestion: Key marketing anchor linking M7 prediction to M6 causal targeting. Pair with an uplift exercise on the Hillstrom data.

Cautions: Metadata confirmed through Crossref. I didn't verify an open-access copy.

Rights or Access: library

---

### additional:hitsch-misra-zhang-targeting | Heterogeneous Treatment Effects and Optimal Targeting Policy Evaluation

Source URL: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3111957

Modules: M6, M7

Priority: recommended

Focus: A framework for building and evaluating customer targeting policies from one randomized dataset using off-policy evaluation. In catalog mailing data, direct CATE methods (including their treatment effect projection) beat outcome-model methods on profit.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor background and an advanced reading on why you evaluate targeting policies by profit, not by prediction accuracy.

Cautions: The SSRN page (revised Nov 2023, first posted 2018) shows no journal. I believe a version appeared in Quantitative Marketing and Economics (2024) but haven't verified it.

Rights or Access: free-registration

---

### additional:kiciman-2023-causal-reasoning-llms | Causal Reasoning and Large Language Models: Opening a New Frontier for Causality

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00050

Modules: M6, AI

Priority: core

Focus: GPT-4-class models do very well on text-based causal tasks (pairwise causal discovery, counterfactuals, necessary/sufficient causes) but show unpredictable failure modes. The authors suggest pairing LLMs, which supply domain knowledge and DAG drafting, with formal causal methods.

Teaching Suggestion: Frames the AI-assisted workflow for M6: let the LLM propose a DAG and confounders, then verify with data and refutation tests (see PyWhy-LLM).

Cautions: By DoWhy contributors (Microsoft Research). Current version v3, Aug 2024.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:cladder-2023 | CLadder: Assessing Causal Reasoning in Language Models

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.04350

Modules: M6, AI

Priority: optional

Focus: A 10K-question benchmark of associational, interventional and counterfactual queries built from causal graphs. LLMs find formal causal inference rules hard, even with a custom CausalCoT prompt.

Teaching Suggestion: Counterpoint to Kıcıman et al.: LLMs talk causality fluently but stumble on formal rung-2/3 reasoning, so students should check identification themselves.

Cautions: The arXiv page lists no venue; widely cited as NeurIPS 2023 (not verified). The companion 'Can Large Language Models Infer Causation from Correlation?' (Corr2Cause; Jin et al., arXiv:2306.05836, https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05836) finds 17 LLMs near random at inferring causation from correlations.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:pywhy-llm | PyWhy-LLM: integrating LLM capabilities into causal analysis

Source URL: https://github.com/py-why/pywhy-llm

Modules: M6, AI

Priority: recommended

Focus: An experimental library that uses LLMs as a stand-in domain expert: it suggests confounders, edges and DAGs, proposes backdoor, mediator and IV sets, and critiques a given DAG with suggested negative controls.

Teaching Suggestion: Exercise: students let PyWhy-LLM (or a chat assistant) propose a DAG for a marketing question, then defend or reject each edge.

Cautions: Experimental; install with `pip install pywhyllm`. No published release shown. No year given.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:horton-homo-silicus | Large Language Models as Simulated Economic Agents: What Can We Learn from Homo Silicus?

Source URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w31122

Modules: AI, M6, M7, M8

Priority: core

Focus: Treats LLMs as implicit computational models of humans ('Homo silicus') that can be given endowments and preferences and run through classic behavioral-economics experiments. Results are broadly similar to the originals.

Teaching Suggestion: Anchor for the debate 'can a simulated experiment replace a real A/B test?'. Students run a small LLM-simulated survey and compare it with real data.

Cautions: Originally sole-authored by Horton (2023); the NBER page now lists three authors and a Feb 2026 revision.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:aher-2023-turing-experiments | Using Large Language Models to Simulate Multiple Humans and Replicate Human Subject Studies

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.10264

Modules: M6, AI

Priority: recommended

Focus: Proposes 'Turing Experiments' that simulate representative samples of participants. Replicates the Ultimatum Game, garden-path sentences and Milgram, but finds a 'hyper-accuracy distortion' in wisdom-of-crowds tasks for newer models.

Teaching Suggestion: Pair with Horton. The hyper-accuracy distortion is a concrete failure mode for simulated consumer panels.

Cautions: First posted 2022; current v5 July 2023. Widely cited as ICML 2023, though the arXiv page lists no venue.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:islp-labs-repo | ISLP_labs: Python lab notebooks for ISLP

Source URL: https://github.com/intro-stat-learning/ISLP_labs

Modules: M7, M3, M4

Priority: core

Focus: Twelve Jupyter notebooks, one per ISLP chapter (Ch02 to Ch13: linreg, classification, resample, baggboost, deeplearning, unsup and so on), with small datasets and a requirements.txt pinned at tag v2.2.2.

Teaching Suggestion: Embed or fork the classification, resampling and baggboost notebooks as Colab in-class coding activities. Students can also ask an AI assistant to explain or extend a lab cell.

Cautions: Labs are versioned (v2.2.2). Pin that tag so the notebooks match the requirements file.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:sklearn-cross-validation | scikit-learn User Guide 3.1: Cross-validation, evaluating estimator performance

Source URL: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/cross_validation.html

Modules: M7

Priority: core

Focus: The canonical reference for cross_val_score and cross_validate, K-fold, stratified, grouped (GroupKFold) and time-series (TimeSeriesSplit) splitters, and permutation tests.

Teaching Suggestion: Link from the M7 'how to evaluate a churn model' page, and use GroupKFold (customers) and TimeSeriesSplit (forecasting) as marketing-relevant splitting examples.

### additional:sklearn-common-pitfalls | scikit-learn User Guide 12: Common pitfalls and recommended practices

Source URL: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html

Modules: M7, AI

Priority: core

Focus: Short worked examples of inconsistent preprocessing, data leakage (for example feature selection on the full data inflates accuracy from 0.5 to about 0.76 on pure noise) and random_state control, with Pipeline as the fix.

Teaching Suggestion: Required reading before students let an AI assistant write an ML pipeline. Use it as an audit checklist: 'find the leakage in this AI-generated notebook'.

Cautions: These are exactly the bugs LLM-written notebooks often contain: fit_transform before the train/test split, and feature selection on the full data.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:neslin-2006-defection-detection | Defection Detection: Measuring and Understanding the Predictive Accuracy of Customer Churn Models

Source URL: https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1509/jmkr.43.2.204

Modules: M7

Priority: core

Focus: Reports a churn-modeling tournament (Teradata Center at Duke) in which many teams modeled the same telecom data. It shows that method choice matters for predictive accuracy and that accuracy translates into substantial retention profit.

Teaching Suggestion: Academic anchor for the churn unit. Use the tournament framing to motivate holdout evaluation (top-decile lift, Gini) on students' own churn models.

Cautions: The tournament detail (Teradata Center at Duke) is from background knowledge and was not verified; the fetched page confirmed only the title, authors, volume and pages. IAOR lists the authors in a different order.

### additional:lemmens-croux-2006-bagging-boosting-churn | Bagging and Boosting Classification Trees to Predict Churn

Source URL: https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1509/jmkr.43.2.276

Modules: M7

Priority: core

Focus: A classic marketing paper showing that ensemble tree methods (bagging, stochastic gradient boosting) beat logistic regression for churn prediction, and discussing how to handle oversampled (balanced) training data.

Teaching Suggestion: Pair it with the XGBoost lab. It is an early marketing-journal case for boosting, and its correction for balanced sampling is a useful discussion point.

Cautions: The Tilburg repository record lists a PDF (lemmens_bagging.pdf), but open access was not confirmed.

### additional:ascarza-2018-retention-review | In Pursuit of Enhanced Customer Retention Management: Review, Key Issues, and Future Directions

Modules: M7, M4

Priority: recommended

Teaching Suggestion: Framing reading for the churn module. It connects M4 (CLV) to M7 (prediction) and M6 (targeting experiments).

### additional:davenport-2011-next-best-offer | Know What Your Customers Want Before They Do

Source URL: https://hbr.org/2011/12/know-what-your-customers-want-before-they-do

Modules: M7

Focus: A managerial article on 'next best offer' (NBO) analytics. It gives a four-step framework (define objectives, gather data, analyze and execute, learn and evolve) with Tesco, Zappos, Microsoft and Walmart examples.

### additional:surprise-recsys | Surprise: a Python scikit for recommender systems

### additional:ms-recommenders | Recommenders: Best Practices on Recommendation Systems

Source URL: https://github.com/recommenders-team/recommenders

Modules: M7

Priority: optional

Focus: A large collection of notebooks and utilities for about 33 recommender algorithms (ALS, BPR, SAR, NCF, LightGCN, SASRec, content-based and others), with data prep, offline evaluation and tuning.

Teaching Suggestion: Source of quick-start notebooks for team projects that want a recommender, and instructor reference for evaluation metrics (precision@k, NDCG).

Rights or Access: open

### additional:netflix-beyond-5-stars | Netflix Recommendations: Beyond the 5 stars (Part 1)

Source URL: https://netflixtechblog.com/netflix-recommendations-beyond-the-5-stars-part-1-55838468f429

Modules: M7, M8

Priority: core

Focus: Netflix's own account of the Netflix Prize. SVD and RBM from the Progress Prize went into production, but the winning ensemble was never deployed because the accuracy gains did not justify the engineering cost, and the business goal shifted from RMSE to engagement and retention.

Teaching Suggestion: Case discussion: offline metric vs business objective. It also pairs with privacy (M8), since the Prize sequel was cancelled after a lawsuit and FTC concerns.

Cautions: For history: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix_Prize (fetched) covers the 2006-2009 timeline, the $1M prize to BellKor's Pragmatic Chaos, the Narayanan-Shmatikov de-anonymization, the 2009 lawsuit and the 2010 cancellation of the sequel.

### additional:mullainathan-spiess-2017 | Machine Learning: An Applied Econometric Approach

Source URL: https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/jep.31.2.87

Modules: M7, M3, M6

Priority: core

Focus: An accessible explanation of how supervised ML differs from econometrics: it is good at prediction (y-hat) but not at recovering parameters (beta-hat), illustrated with house-price prediction and regularization.

Teaching Suggestion: The opening reading for M7, connecting M3 (regression) and M6 (causal) to prediction.

Cautions: JEP offers a free PDF. Replication data is on openICPSR (project 113993, seen in search).

Rights or Access: open

### additional:mle-bench | MLE-bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Machine Learning Engineering

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07095

Modules: M7, AI

Priority: recommended

Focus: A benchmark of 75 Kaggle competitions for AI agents. o1-preview with AIDE scaffolding reached medal level in 16.9% of competitions at release, and agents on the repo's paused leaderboard now score above 60%.

Teaching Suggestion: Discussion of how far 'AI does the ML for you' has come. Show the leaderboard and the rule-violation and plagiarism detectors as evidence of how agents can cheat.

### additional:kapoor-narayanan-leakage | Leakage and the Reproducibility Crisis in ML-based Science

Source URL: https://reproducible.cs.princeton.edu/

Modules: M7, AI

Priority: core

Focus: Documents leakage errors in hundreds of ML-based papers across many fields, gives an eight-type leakage taxonomy, and proposes 'model info sheets' to rule leakage out.

Teaching Suggestion: Use the taxonomy and model info sheet as a required appendix in student project write-ups, especially when AI wrote the pipeline.

Cautions: The project page links the Patterns 2023 paper and keeps a table (updated May 2024) of 41 papers across 30 fields that document leakage errors, which together affect 648 papers.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:yang-2022-notebook-leakage | Data Leakage in Notebooks: Static Detection and Better Processes

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.03345

Modules: M7, AI

Priority: optional

Focus: A static-analysis tool that detects common train/test leakage patterns in data-science notebooks. Leakage turns out to be widespread across more than 100,000 public notebooks, and the paper discusses processes to prevent it.

Teaching Suggestion: Evidence that leakage is the default failure in notebook code, which is also what LLMs learn from. Motivates the course rule: always split first and use a Pipeline.

Cautions: arXiv lists no journal reference. I believe it appeared at ASE 2022, but that venue is unverified.

Rights or Access: open

Modules: M7, AI

Focus: Three lines of code (TabularPredictor.fit) train and stack many models on a tabular dataset. It comes with a ready Colab notebook.

### additional:tabpfn | TabPFN: Accurate predictions on small data with a tabular foundation model

Source URL: https://github.com/PriorLabs/TabPFN

Modules: M7, AI

Priority: optional

Focus: A pretrained transformer that does classification and regression on small tabular datasets in one forward pass, with no tuning, through a scikit-learn-style API. It is often competitive with tuned boosting.

Teaching Suggestion: Shows where 'foundation models' are heading for tabular marketing data. Students drop TabPFNClassifier into their churn pipeline and compare it with XGBoost.

Cautions: The Nature page fetch failed; the DOI and title come from the GitHub README. TabPFN-2.5 and later weights are non-commercial (fine for class use). It needs a GPU for larger data.

### additional:lambrecht-tucker-2019-algorithmic-bias | Algorithmic Bias? An Empirical Study of Apparent Gender-Based Discrimination in the Display of STEM Career Ads

Source URL: https://ideas.repec.org/a/inm/ormnsc/v65y2019i7p2966-2981.html

Modules: M8, M6

Priority: core

Focus: A gender-neutral STEM job ad was shown to fewer women because younger women are a more expensive audience. Cost-minimizing delivery produced the apparent bias, and the pattern held across platforms.

Teaching Suggestion: Core case for algorithmic bias arising from market mechanics rather than intent, discussed alongside Ali et al. (2019).

Rights or Access: library

### additional:ali-2019-discrimination-through-optimization | Discrimination through optimization: How Facebook's ad delivery can lead to skewed outcomes

Source URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.02095

Modules: M8, AI

Priority: core

Focus: Paired ad experiments show that Facebook's delivery optimization skews employment and housing ads by gender and race even with neutral targeting, driven by budget effects and the platform's predicted relevance of the ad content.

Teaching Suggestion: Pair with Lambrecht and Tucker: one shows a market-cost mechanism, the other a platform-prediction mechanism. Good for a debate on who is accountable.

Cautions: The venue (PACM HCI/CSCW) is inferred from the ACM DOI listed on arXiv.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:calvano-2020-ai-pricing-collusion | Artificial Intelligence, Algorithmic Pricing, and Collusion

Source URL: https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.20190623

Modules: M8, AI

Priority: recommended

Focus: Q-learning pricing algorithms in simulated oligopolies learn to sustain supra-competitive prices with punishment strategies, without communicating.

Teaching Suggestion: Background for the algorithmic-pricing discussion (RealPage-style cases). Present the key figure and intuition rather than assigning the full paper.

Cautions: Empirical complement: Brown & MacKay (2023), 'Competition in Pricing Algorithms', AEJ: Microeconomics 15(2): 109-56, doi 10.1257/mic.20210158 (aeaweb page verified). It shows that simple rival-responsive pricing algorithms at online retailers can raise prices.

Rights or Access: library

Modules: M5, M8

Priority: recommended

Focus: Integrative review and framework for influencer marketing: influencer, follower, content and brand factors and how they drive engagement and sales. Won the 2022 JAMS Sheth Foundation Best Paper Award.

Teaching Suggestion: Framework reading for influencer analytics; pairs with the MBA 542 TikTok transcript exercise, in which an LLM scores expertise and authenticity cues.

Cautions: Also on the MBA 542 Module 3 reading list. Distinct from the Leung et al. (2022) Journal of Marketing paper on influencer marketing effectiveness, which is also in this catalog.

Rights or Access: library

### additional:chintala-liaukonyte-yang-2024-browsing-aisles-app | Browsing the Aisles or Browsing the App? How Online Grocery Shopping is Changing What We Buy

Source URL: https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/mksc.2022.0292

Modules: M2, M6, M4

Priority: core

Focus: Household panel evidence on how the same shoppers' baskets differ when they buy groceries online versus in store: fewer impulse and unhealthy items and more repetition online, with implications for new-product introduction.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor's own paper; a natural M2/M6 case. Pairs with the synthetic Instacart vs. in-person grocery data used in MBA 542 Module 1.

Cautions: Also on the MBA 542 Module 1 reading list. The summary is high-level; check the wording against the published abstract before quoting it on the wiki.

Rights or Access: library

### additional:narang-shankar-2019-mobile-app | Mobile App Introduction and Online and Offline Purchases and Product Returns

Source URL: https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/mksc.2019.1169

Modules: M6, M2

Priority: recommended

Focus: Estimates how adopting a retailer's mobile app changes customers' online and offline purchases and product returns, using a quasi-experimental design that compares adopters with matched non-adopters.

Teaching Suggestion: A marketing quasi-experiment by the course's previous instructor; useful continuity for students and a clean worked example of difference-in-differences with matching.

Cautions: Also on the MBA 542 Module 1 reading list.

Modules: M7, M1

### additional:shani-gunawardana-2011-evaluating-recsys | Evaluating Recommendation Systems

### additional:adomavicius-2019-recsys-biases | Reducing Recommender System Biases: An Investigation of Rating Display Designs

Source URL: https://misq.org/reeducing-recommender-system-biases-an-investigation-of-rating-display-designs.html

Modules: M7, M6

Priority: optional

Focus: Experiments show that displayed recommendation ratings anchor consumers' own ratings, and test display designs that reduce the bias. Recommenders thereby shape the very data they are later trained on.

Teaching Suggestion: Discussion reading on feedback loops between recommendation and measurement; ties M7 to M6.

Cautions: Also on the MBA 542 Module 5 reading list. The MISQ URL contains a typo ('reeducing') on the publisher's own site.

Rights or Access: library

### additional:chawla-2002-smote | SMOTE: Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique

Source URL: https://jair.org/index.php/jair/article/view/10302

Modules: M7

Priority: optional

Focus: Introduces oversampling of rare classes by interpolating synthetic minority examples, a standard tool for churn and response models where positives are rare.

Teaching Suggestion: Background for an imbalanced-churn exercise. Also a good AI-coding check: oversampling before the train/test split leaks information, and AI-written pipelines often make that mistake.

Cautions: Also on the MBA 542 Module 8 reading list. In practice, class weights or threshold tuning often work as well as SMOTE.

Rights or Access: open

Focus: Compares AI-generated with human-made marketing images at scale, finding that current generative models can match or exceed human-made visuals on quality and realism measures.

### additional:github-pages-limits | GitHub Pages limits

Source URL: https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits

Modules: WIKI

Priority: core

Focus: Official GitHub Pages limits: a published site can be at most 1 GB, and the source repo should stay under 1 GB. Soft limits are 100 GB/month of bandwidth and 10 builds/hour (custom GitHub Actions builds are exempt), and deployments time out after 10 minutes. Pages is not meant for commercial or sensitive-transaction sites.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor-only planning: keep the wiki's datasets and media under these caps, host large data elsewhere (GitHub Releases, Box, Hugging Face), and never collect passwords or student data on the site.

Cautions: Rate-limited requests get HTTP 429. Custom domains use a CNAME record for a subdomain or A/ALIAS/ANAME for an apex domain; verify the domain first to prevent takeover (https://docs.github.com/en/pages/configuring-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site/about-custom-domains-and-github-pages, fetched). A campus subdomain such as *.illinois.edu would need campus DNS cooperation; that is my inference, not from GitHub's docs.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:github-pages-custom-workflows | Using custom workflows with GitHub Pages

Source URL: https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/using-custom-workflows-with-github-pages

Modules: WIKI

Priority: core

Focus: How to build and deploy a Pages site with GitHub Actions using actions/configure-pages@v5, actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4 and actions/deploy-pages@v4 (the examples also use actions/checkout@v6). The deploy job needs the pages: write and id-token: write permissions.

Teaching Suggestion: Reference for the wiki's build pipeline; Quarto, Jupyter Book 2, marimo and JupyterLite sites all deploy this way.

Cautions: The artifact must be a gzipped tar under 10 GB with no symbolic or hard links. Action versions are as shown on 2026-10-23; pin them in the workflow file.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:github-classroom-deprecated | GitHub Classroom deprecated

Source URL: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-08-27-github-classroom-deprecated

Modules: WIKI

Priority: core

Focus: GitHub Classroom shut down on 2026-08-28, including its website, APIs and services. Classroom and assignment names, tests defined outside repos and LTI rosters will be deleted; user accounts, repos and organizations stay.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor-only: don't build BADM 534's assignment distribution on GitHub Classroom. Use Classroom 50, Codio, or plain template repositories instead.

Cautions: New sign-ups ended 2026-05-26 (https://github.blog/changelog/2026-05-26-github-classroom-sign-ups-are-no-longer-available, fetched). GitHub's migration page names Codio and Classroom 50 as partner options and describes a gh CLI export utility (https://docs.github.com/en/education/manage-coursework-with-github-classroom/get-started-with-github-classroom/export-or-migrate-github-classroom-data, fetched). Older GitHub Education pages still describe Classroom as active and are stale.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:classroom50 | Classroom 50

Source URL: https://www.classroom50.org/

Modules: WIKI

Priority: recommended

Focus: Free, open-source replacement for GitHub Classroom that distributes and autogrades programming assignments in GitHub repos. Features include template repos, due dates, individual or group work, pytest or input/output tests, CSV rosters and score export.

Teaching Suggestion: Candidate tool for handing out starter notebooks and programming assignments through GitHub, linked from the wiki's assignment pages.

Cautions: The sponsoring organization and the feature list come from a third-party blog (https://bruceelgort.com/2026/07/20/github-classroom-is-gone-heres-the-free-tool-that-replaces-it/, fetched); the official homepage only says it is the free, open-source alternative to GitHub Classroom, with no license named. It needs a GitHub organization on a Team plan (free for verified educators) and broad read/write access to the org's repos. It reached general availability on 2026-07-01 per GitHub's migration doc. It is new, so pilot it before relying on it.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:github-education-teachers | About GitHub Education for teachers

Source URL: https://docs.github.com/en/education/about-github-education/github-education-for-teachers/about-github-education-for-teachers

### additional:netlify-cloudflare-alternatives | Netlify pricing update: introducing credit-based plans

Source URL: https://www.netlify.com/changelog/netlify-pricing-update-introducing-credit-based-plans/

Modules: WIKI

Priority: optional

Focus: Since 2025-09-05, Netlify plans run on credits. The free plan gives 300 credits a month. Each production deploy costs 15 credits, bandwidth 10 credits per GB, and web requests 3 credits per 10,000; preview deploys are free.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor-only comparison: at 15 credits per production deploy, a free Netlify site allows at most about 20 deploys a month even before bandwidth. That is tight for a wiki updated often; GitHub Pages has no such meter.

Cautions: Cloudflare Pages' free plan allows 500 builds a month, 20,000 files per site and 25 MiB per file (https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/platform/limits, fetched). Both hosts offer deploy previews, which GitHub Pages lacks. Netlify's changelog does not say what happens when free credits run out.

Rights or Access: freemium

### additional:quarto | Quarto

Source URL: https://quarto.org/

Modules: WIKI, AI

Priority: core

Focus: Open-source, Pandoc-based publishing system that turns .qmd, .ipynb and Markdown files containing Python or R code into websites, books, slides and PDFs. Websites get navigation, cross-references and a built-in local search index.

Teaching Suggestion: Leading candidate engine for the BADM 534 wiki. One source produces pages, slides and notebooks, and freeze means heavy Python runs only on the instructor's machine.

Cautions: Version status on 2026-10-23: 1.10.x is the current stable line (GitHub marks v1.10.18 as Latest, July 2026), and 1.11.x is in pre-release. Quarto 1.9 (2026-03-24, https://opensource.posit.co/blog/2026-03-24_1.9-release/, fetched) added 'llms-txt: true' for websites, which writes an llms.txt index plus a .llms.md copy of each page so students can feed the wiki to an AI assistant. It also made opt-in (express) cookie consent the default, added screen-reader labels for videos, and added experimental PDF/UA output. Release posts now live on opensource.posit.co. Algolia is an optional alternative to the built-in search.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:quarto-publish-github-pages | Quarto: GitHub Pages publishing guide

Source URL: https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages

Modules: WIKI

Priority: core

Focus: Covers three ways to publish: render to a docs/ folder, run 'quarto publish gh-pages', or use a GitHub Action (quarto-dev/quarto-actions/publish@v2). Also explains 'execute: freeze: auto', which runs code locally and commits the results in _freeze.

Teaching Suggestion: Step-by-step deployment for a Quarto wiki. Freeze avoids rebuilding Python environments in CI on every commit.

Cautions: Add a .nojekyll file when publishing from docs/. The Action route needs read/write workflow permissions.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:quarto-live | Quarto Live: interactive code blocks and exercises (webR and Pyodide)

Source URL: https://r-wasm.github.io/quarto-live/

Modules: WIKI

Priority: core

Focus: Quarto extension that adds editable, runnable R (webR) and Python (Pyodide) code blocks to HTML pages. It supports exercises with blanks, hints, solutions and custom grading, all running in the browser on any static host such as GitHub Pages.

Teaching Suggestion: Embed in-browser Python practice cells and auto-checked exercises in wiki pages so students can try code without Colab or a local install.

Cautions: The 0.1.1 announcement (https://tidyverse.org/blog/2024/10/quarto-live-0-1-1/, fetched) explains exercise, setup and check blocks. The repo (https://github.com/r-wasm/quarto-live, MIT) has no tagged releases and shows a 0.1.2-dev version. The docs site was rebuilt with Quarto 1.9.38 in 2026, but recent commit dates could not be confirmed, so treat it as early-stage (0.x). The community alternative coatless-quarto/pyodide (https://github.com/coatless-quarto/pyodide) itself points users to quarto-live as the official option.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:shortiquiz | shortiquiz: interactive quiz questions for Quarto HTML documents

Source URL: https://github.com/skyfroger/shortiquiz

Modules: WIKI

Priority: recommended

Focus: Quarto extension offering multiple-choice, multi-answer, text-input, dropdown, Parsons (reorder lines of code), image-hotspot, flashcard and gated-stage questions. Install with 'quarto add skyfroger/shortiquiz'.

Teaching Suggestion: Low-stakes self-checks at the end of each module page. Parsons problems suit code-reading practice for non-CS students checking AI-generated code.

Cautions: GPL-3.0 copyleft applies to the extension code shipped with the site. The repo has 59 commits; the last-commit date was not visible. Answers sit in the page source, so use it for ungraded practice only and keep graded quizzes in Canvas.

### additional:jupyter-book-2 | Jupyter Book 2

Source URL: https://jupyterbook.org/

Modules: WIKI

Priority: core

Focus: Jupyter Book 2 was released the week of 2025-11-04, keeping the jupyter-book package name, and is rebuilt on the MyST Document Engine. Authors write in notebooks or MyST Markdown and get cross-references, build-time execution, and interactivity in the browser or through Binder/JupyterHub.

Teaching Suggestion: Strong alternative to Quarto if the wiki is notebook-first; it is the stack behind the Data 8 textbook and QuantEcon-style lecture sites.

Cautions: Known limitations versus v1 (https://jupyterbook.org/stable/resources/faq, fetched): pretty URLs, so my_page.html becomes /my-page/; myst.yml replaces _config.yml; not yet at parity on execution features, editable Thebe cells or autodoc. The v1 Sphinx stack is 'mostly in maintenance mode'; pin jupyter-book<2 to stay on v1. Release rationale: https://jupyterbook.org/blog/posts/2025-11-04-why-make-a-major-release. The blog shows active 2026 development: mystmd 1.8.2 (Mar 2026), an AnyWidget directive (Mar 2026), accessibility work on the MyST theme (May 2026), a 'Demystifying MyST Markdown in Education' event (Apr 2026) and a new release (Sep 2026).

Rights or Access: open

### additional:zensical | Zensical

Source URL: https://zensical.org/

Modules: WIKI

Priority: optional

Focus: Successor static site generator from the makers of Material for MkDocs. It reads existing mkdocs.yml projects and adds faster differential rebuilds and a new client-side search engine (Disco).

Teaching Suggestion: Keep on the watch list if a Markdown-only docs look is preferred; it is too young to be the main engine for an upcoming semester.

Cautions: Status on 2026-10-23: pre-0.1 (the site is built with zensical 0.0.70). A 'dependable release line' starting with 0.1 is scheduled for 2026-11-05. Only a subset of MkDocs plugins is supported. An October 2026 update says the planned Rust Markdown parser has been replaced by a Python-Markdown-compatible one. Announcement: https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2025/11/05/zensical/. It has no notebook-execution story comparable to Quarto or MyST.

### additional:pyodide | Pyodide changelog

Source URL: https://pyodide.org/en/stable/project/changelog.html

Modules: WIKI

Priority: recommended

Focus: Pyodide, CPython compiled to WebAssembly, is the engine under quarto-live, JupyterLite, marimo WASM and PyScript. The 314.x line (314.0.0 on 2026-06-09) runs Python 3.14, and 314.0.7 (2026-09-14) is the latest release.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor-only reference for which Python version and package builds students get in any in-browser cell.

Cautions: Version numbers jumped from 0.x (0.28 shipped Python 3.13) to 314.x. The changelog announces no policy, so the link to the Python version is my inference. 0.29.5 and 0.27.8 got Node 26 fixes in September 2026. Pure-Python wheels install through micropip.

### additional:pyodide-packages | Packages built in Pyodide

Source URL: https://pyodide.org/en/stable/usage/packages-in-pyodide.html

Modules: WIKI, M2, M3, M4, M7

Priority: core

Focus: List of compiled packages shipped with Pyodide 314.0.7, including pandas 3.0.2, scikit-learn 1.8.0, statsmodels 0.14.6, scipy 1.18.0, matplotlib 3.10.8 and numpy 2.4.6. Seaborn is not on the built-in list.

Teaching Suggestion: Check before writing in-browser exercises: the core M2–M7 stack (pandas wrangling, statsmodels OLS/logit, scikit-learn clustering and prediction) runs in the browser.

Cautions: Trade-offs: the first page load downloads the runtime and packages. marimo's docs cite a 2 GB memory cap and no true threading or multiprocessing under WASM. Packages with compiled code that are not on this list (for example PyTorch) generally won't install. Seaborn is pure Python and should install through micropip (not tested). pandas 3.0 is a major release, so syntax can differ from older tutorials and from whatever pandas version Colab ships; check version parity before mixing Colab and in-browser cells.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:jupyterlite | JupyterLite documentation

Source URL: https://jupyterlite.readthedocs.io/en/stable/

Modules: WIKI

Priority: core

Focus: A JupyterLab and Notebook distribution that runs entirely in the browser, with Pyodide or Xeus Python kernels in Web Workers. It deploys as a static site with no server.

Teaching Suggestion: Give students a full notebook interface from a wiki link (for example a 'Try it' button on each module) with no accounts or installs.

Cautions: The docs were labeled 0.8.6 when fetched, while their compatibility table listed jupyterlite-core 0.7.0 (bundling JupyterLab 4.5 and Notebook 7.5); confirm the current version before pinning. Only the last two releases are supported. Not every JupyterLab feature works. Student files are kept in browser storage, so test how work persists before relying on it for assignments.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:jupyterlite-demo-template | jupyterlite/demo: template for deploying JupyterLite to GitHub Pages

Source URL: https://github.com/jupyterlite/demo

Modules: WIKI

Priority: core

Focus: Template repo that builds a JupyterLite site and deploys it to GitHub Pages with GitHub Actions. Notebooks go in the content folder, and kernels and extensions are listed in requirements.txt.

Teaching Suggestion: Use as the template for a BADM 534 'lab' subsite that holds the module notebooks and is linked from the wiki.

Cautions: Deploy guide (https://jupyterlite.readthedocs.io/en/stable/quickstart/deploy.html, fetched): click 'Use this template', enable Actions, set workflow permissions to read/write and the Pages source to GitHub Actions. For pre-installed packages, use the xeus-python demo with an environment.yml. Live demo at jupyterlite.github.io/demo. Requires Firefox 90+ or Chromium 89+.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:marimo-wasm | marimo WebAssembly notebooks

Source URL: https://docs.marimo.io/guides/wasm/

Modules: WIKI, M4

Priority: core

Focus: marimo's reactive notebooks can run entirely in the browser through Pyodide. numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pandas and matplotlib are pre-installed, and other pure-Python wheels install automatically on import.

Teaching Suggestion: Build reactive demos (for example sliders driving a CLV or conjoint simulator), export them as static HTML, and embed them in wiki pages.

Cautions: Export with 'marimo export html-wasm notebook.py -o out --mode run' for a read-only app or '--mode edit' for an editable notebook. The export must be served over HTTP, not opened from file://, and Pyodide and packages load from a CDN. Run 'marimo check --select MW' to catch incompatible packages (https://docs.marimo.io/guides/exporting/webassembly_html/, fetched). Limits: 2 GB memory, emulated concurrency, no PDB. marimo islands, which embed single reactive cells in any HTML page, are still a 'Preview' feature (https://docs.marimo.io/guides/island_example/, fetched).

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:marimo-ai-notebook | marimo: reactive Python notebook (GitHub repository)

Source URL: https://github.com/marimo-team/marimo

Modules: WIKI, AI

Priority: recommended

Focus: Open-source reactive Python notebook stored as plain .py files. It has a built-in AI assistant that sees in-memory variables, Copilot completion, bring-your-own-key or local models, and 'marimo pair' for working alongside Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode.

Teaching Suggestion: Option for in-class vibe-coding activities: notebooks diff cleanly in Git and work with coding agents, and the same files export to WASM pages for the wiki.

Cautions: 22.3k stars when fetched. The latest release number was not visible on the fetched page.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:pyscript | PyScript

Source URL: https://pyscript.net/

Modules: WIKI

Priority: optional

Focus: Open-source platform for running Python inside web pages. The current release is 2026.7.3 (year-based version numbers), with docs at pyscript.github.io/docs/latest/.

Teaching Suggestion: Optional for hand-built plain-HTML widgets; for course notebooks, quarto-live, JupyterLite or marimo are more turnkey.

Cautions: The fetched homepage names neither its runtimes nor its license; check the docs before adopting.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:binder-thebe | Binder (mybinder.org) user guidelines

Source URL: https://mybinder.readthedocs.io/en/latest/about/user-guidelines.html

Modules: WIKI

Priority: optional

Focus: Free service that launches a GitHub repo of notebooks in a temporary cloud Jupyter session. Sessions get 1–2 GB of RAM, shut down after 10 minutes idle, last up to about 6 hours, and are capped at 100 simultaneous users per repository.

Teaching Suggestion: Fallback 'Launch Binder' button for notebooks that need packages Pyodide lacks. The 100-user cap and slow cold starts make it unreliable for a whole class at once.

Cautions: The mybinder.org homepage says the service is 'currently in testing'. Thebe (https://github.com/jupyter-book/thebe, BSD-3-Clause, fetched) turns static code cells into runnable ones backed by a Jupyter server, or by JupyterLite through thebe-lite. Thebe 0.9.0 is still in development, and Jupyter Book 2 does not yet support editable Thebe cells.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:colab-github-badge | Using Google Colab with GitHub (colab-github-demo notebook)

Source URL: https://github.com/googlecolab/colabtools/blob/main/notebooks/colab-github-demo.ipynb

Modules: WIKI, M1

Priority: core

Focus: Official Colab notebook explaining the colab.research.google.com/github/<org>/<repo>/blob/<branch>/<path>.ipynb URL pattern and the 'Open In Colab' badge in Markdown and HTML. It also covers saving copies to Drive or back to GitHub, and access to private repos.

Teaching Suggestion: Put an Open in Colab badge on every wiki notebook so students can run the full analysis (with Gemini in Colab) on Google's servers.

Cautions: Colab opens an editable copy and leaves the repo unchanged. Saving back to GitHub requires granting Colab permission to push commits. The notebook text was read from the raw.githubusercontent.com copy.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:h5p | H5P

Source URL: https://h5p.org/

Modules: WIKI

Priority: optional

Focus: Open HTML5 framework (MIT) for interactive content such as interactive video, presentations and quiz-style games. The paid H5P.com service adds LTI integration with Canvas and other LMSs.

Teaching Suggestion: Optional for richer self-checks. On a static site, h5p-standalone (https://github.com/tunapanda/h5p-standalone, MIT, 3.x) plays .h5p packages without a server.

Cautions: Authoring needs an H5P-enabled platform or H5P.com. The paid Premium tier adds AI-powered 'Smart Import'. Content embedded in a GitHub Pages wiki sends no grades back, so keep graded quizzes in Canvas.

Rights or Access: freemium

### additional:mlu-explain | MLU-Explain

Source URL: https://mlu-explain.github.io/

Modules: M3, M7, WIKI

Priority: core

Focus: Interactive scrollytelling explainers covering linear and logistic regression, train/test/validation splits, cross-validation, precision and recall, ROC/AUC, decision trees, random forests, the bias-variance trade-off and double descent.

Teaching Suggestion: Link or assign from the M3 and M7 pages; also a model for the visual-explainer style the wiki could adopt.

Cautions: The GitHub repo was archived (read-only) on 2026-03-06, so expect no more updates; the site still loads. The site lists 14 articles and the repo holds 10.

Rights or Access: open

### additional:seeing-theory | Seeing Theory

Source URL: https://seeing-theory.brown.edu/

Modules: M3, M6, WIKI

Priority: recommended

Focus: Brown University's D3-based visual introduction to probability and statistics. It runs from basic probability through distributions, frequentist and Bayesian inference, and regression.

Teaching Suggestion: Refresher links on the M3 (regression) and M6 (inference) pages for students who are rusty on statistics.

Cautions: The site is now archived for reference. The page states no license. Source: https://github.com/seeingtheory/Seeing-Theory (license not checked).

### additional:observable-framework | Observable Framework

Source URL: https://observablehq.github.io/framework/

Modules: M2, WIKI

Priority: optional

Focus: Open-source static site generator for data apps, dashboards and reports. Pages are Markdown with reactive JavaScript, and data loaders written in Python, R or SQL snapshot the data at build time.

Teaching Suggestion: Option for interactive dashboards inside the wiki (for example a customer-segmentation explorer) where Python prepares the data at build time.

Cautions: v1.13.4 per the site. The docs now live at observablehq.github.io/framework, and observablehq.com/framework redirects there. No maintenance notice was seen, but check recent activity before committing. Repo: https://github.com/observablehq/framework (ISC).

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:pagefind | Pagefind

Source URL: https://pagefind.app/

Modules: WIKI

Priority: recommended

Focus: Static search library that indexes the built HTML from any site generator and serves a chunked index. It claims a total payload under 300 kB for a full-text search of a 10,000-page site. The current version is 1.5.2.

Teaching Suggestion: Adds search to a plain-HTML or mixed-tool wiki; it is also Starlight's default search.

Cautions: Repo: https://github.com/pagefind/pagefind (MIT). Lunr.js (https://github.com/olivernn/lunr.js, MIT, fetched) is the older in-browser alternative; it shows 105 open issues and recent activity could not be confirmed. Quarto and Jupyter Book 2 have built-in search, so Pagefind matters mainly for plain-HTML builds.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:wcag-overview | WCAG 2 Overview

Source URL: https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/

Modules: WIKI

Priority: core

Focus: W3C overview of WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 and the A, AA and AAA conformance levels. W3C recommends WCAG 2.2, which is backward compatible with 2.1 and is also published as ISO/IEC 40500:2025.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor-only reference for setting the wiki's accessibility target.

Cautions: WCAG 2.1 was last updated 2025-05-06, and WCAG 3 is still an early draft. UIUC's own standard requires 2.2 AA for internally built web content (see uiuc-minimum-digital-accessibility-standards).

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:webaim-wcag-checklist | WebAIM's WCAG 2 Checklist

Source URL: https://webaim.org/standards/wcag/checklist

Modules: WIKI

Priority: core

Focus: Plain-language checklist of the WCAG 2.2 success criteria at levels A, AA and AAA, with filters for 2.0 and 2.1.

Teaching Suggestion: QA checklist to run before each module page goes live: alt text, captions, 4.5:1 contrast, keyboard access, real headings, a lang attribute, and reflow at 200% zoom.

Cautions: Last updated 2024-06-20. Interactive widgets (quizzes, sliders, in-browser code editors) need separate keyboard and screen-reader testing.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:ada-title-ii-web-rule | ADA.gov fact sheet: Title II rule on web content and mobile app accessibility

Source URL: https://www.ada.gov/resources/2024-03-08-web-rule/

Modules: WIKI

Priority: core

Focus: The DOJ's ADA Title II rule requires web content from state and local governments, including public universities, to meet WCAG 2.1 AA. An April 2026 interim final rule moved compliance to 2027-04-26 for entities serving 50,000+ people and 2028-04-26 for smaller ones.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor-only: a public-university course wiki should meet WCAG 2.1 AA by April 2027 at the latest.

Cautions: The exceptions for archived content and individualized password-protected documents are narrow and don't cover public HTML course pages. This is a summary, not legal advice. The page title shown here is paraphrased.

Rights or Access: open

---

### additional:uiuc-minimum-digital-accessibility-standards | University of Illinois Minimum Digital Accessibility Standards

Source URL: https://access.illinois.edu/ada/digital-accessibility-policy/minimum-standards/

Modules: WIKI

Priority: core

Focus: Campus standard under the Digital Accessibility Policy (HR-86). Internally developed web content must meet the most recent recommended WCAG, currently 2.2 AA, use WAI-ARIA 1.2, and work with major browsers and screen readers. Course content and training materials are explicitly in scope.

Teaching Suggestion: The binding target for the BADM 534 wiki: design to WCAG 2.2 AA and test with NVDA and VoiceOver.

Cautions: Commercial SaaS is held to 2.1 AA. Campus resources: instructor tips at https://itaccessibility.illinois.edu/tips-instructor and evaluation tools at https://itaccessibility.illinois.edu/web-evaluation-tools (links seen on itaccessibility.illinois.edu). The page lists no deadlines.

Rights or Access: open

The program site ubc-mds.github.io is built with Hugo.

### additional:teaching-learning-with-jupyter | Teaching and Learning with Jupyter

Source URL: https://jupyter4edu.github.io/jupyter-edu-book/

Modules: WIKI

Priority: recommended

Focus: Open handbook on teaching with Jupyter. It includes a catalogue of 23 pedagogical patterns (for example 'Shift-Enter for the win', 'Fill in the blanks' and test-driven development) and practical chapters on running a class.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor-only guide for structuring in-class coding activities and notebook exercises on the wiki.

Cautions: Built with bookdown/GitBook rather than Jupyter Book. Written in 2019, before AI coding assistants.

### additional:illinois-chat | Illinois Chat (formerly UIUC.chat) documentation

Source URL: https://docs.uiuc.chat/

Modules: AI, WIKI

Priority: core

Focus: Campus-supported platform for building course chatbots over uploaded materials (PDFs, slides, videos, a web crawl, or a Canvas connection). Answers cite their sources, and a tutor-mode prompt is available. The official instance is chat.illinois.edu.

Teaching Suggestion: Build a BADM 534 assistant grounded in the wiki by crawling the GitHub Pages site, and link it from every page.

Cautions: UIUC.chat is moving to chat.illinois.edu, and chatbot creation is disabled on the old site (https://docs.uiuc.chat/migration/migrate-to-illinois-chat.md, fetched). Per the FAQ it is free to use but you supply your own OpenAI API key, and data is stored on AWS with no guarantees; the FAQ may predate the campus migration. Privacy: there is no FERPA statement and no documented iframe embed, so keep student records and grades out of it. Backend: https://github.com/Center-for-AI-Innovation/ai-ta-backend (public, MIT); access to the frontend repo appears restricted. Support: genaisupport@mx.uillinois.edu.

Rights or Access: free-registration

### additional:cs50-ai-duck | CS50.ai (CS50 Duck)

Source URL: https://cs50.ai/

Modules: AI, WIKI

Priority: optional

Focus: CS50's ChatGPT-based 'duck debugger' for students and teachers, supported by Microsoft and OpenAI. It is the best-known example of a course-specific AI tutor.

Teaching Suggestion: Instructor-only model for an AI-help policy and tutor design (guide students rather than solve for them).

Cautions: The fetched page describes neither its guardrails nor whether courses outside CS50 can use it. A CS50 team paper at SIGCSE 2024 describes the design, but I did not verify its URL.

Rights or Access: free-registration
